definition_en: an area of activity, control or knowledge, or the highest rank in the three-domain classification of life
core_image: 一位研究者在自己的书桌前工作了三十年，别的领域的问题也常被送到这张桌上
scene: 一位研究者在自己的领域里工作了三十年，别的学科的问题也常被送到他的桌前。 A researcher worked for thirty years within his own domain, and questions from other fields were often brought to his desk.
sceneCN: 这里 domain 是「领域」（第 1 个义项：活动或知识的范围）；句意：一位研究者在自己的领域里工作了三十年，别的学科的问题也常被送到他的桌前。

pos.zh: 领域；域（生物分类）；域名；定义域；领地；结构域；论域

senses.title: A sphere of activity or knowledge
senses.definition: an area of work, study or responsibility that a person or group occupies
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体所从事的工作、研究或职责范围
senses.example: The researcher worked for thirty years within his own domain.
senses.exampleCN: 这位研究者在自己的领域里工作了三十年。
senses.why: Latin dominium meant 'ownership, lordship'; a domain is first a place where one has authority, then any area one treats as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dominium 意为「所有权、主权」；领域首先是某人有权力的地方，后指某人视作自己地盘的任何范围。

senses.title: The highest rank: domain
senses.definition: in the three-domain scheme, the rank above kingdom, based on fundamental differences in cell type
senses.definitionCN: 三域方案中位于界之上的阶元，依据细胞类型的根本差异划分
senses.example: The three-domain scheme placed the archaea in a domain of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 三域方案把古菌放进它们自己的一个域。
senses.why: Molecular data showed two deeply different prokaryotic groups, so the top of the ladder needed a new name; domain, the word for jurisdiction, was available.
senses.whyCN: 分子数据显出两个差异极深的原核类群，梯子顶端因此需要新名称；表示管辖范围的 domain 正好可用。

senses.title: An internet domain name
senses.definition: the registered address of a website or service, made of a name and a top-level suffix
senses.definitionCN: 网站或服务注册的地址，由一个名称与顶级后缀构成
senses.example: The domain was registered before the product had a name.
senses.exampleCN: 在产品还没有名字之前，域名就已注册。
senses.why: The internet borrowed the word for a bounded address space: whoever holds the name governs that corner of the network, exactly as a lord governs a domain.
senses.whyCN: 互联网借用这个词来指一个有边界的地址空间：持有名称者管辖网络的这个角落，正如领主管辖领地。

senses.title: The domain of a mathematical function
senses.definition: the set of input values for which a function is defined
senses.definitionCN: 使函数有定义的输入值的集合
senses.example: The domain excludes zero, where the function has no value.
senses.exampleCN: 定义域排除零，因为函数在零处无定义。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the 'area of authority' image in a precise form: the domain is where the function is allowed to act.
senses.whyCN: 数学以精确形式保留了「权辖范围」的意象：定义域就是函数被允许起作用的地方。

senses.title: Eminent domain in law
senses.definition: the power of the state to take private property for public use, with compensation
senses.definitionCN: 国家为公共用途、在给予补偿的前提下取得私有财产的权力
senses.example: The city used eminent domain to acquire the strip of land.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府用征用权取得了那条狭长土地。
senses.why: Law made the lordship literal: the state's ultimate domain over land can override a private owner, provided compensation is paid.
senses.whyCN: 法律把领主权字面化：国家对土地的终极管辖可以压过私人所有者，前提是给予补偿。

senses.title: A feudal domain or demesne
senses.definition: land held and governed by a lord, especially the portion kept for his own use
senses.definitionCN: 由领主拥有并治理的土地，尤指保留自用的那部分
senses.example: The manor's domain supplied the household with grain.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园的领地供给这个家户粮食。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: land a lord holds and rules, from which the abstract senses of ownership and sphere later grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：领主拥有并治理的土地；所有权与范围的抽象义后来由此生长。

senses.title: A protein domain
senses.definition: a compact, independently folding part of a protein that performs a specific function
senses.definitionCN: 蛋白质中能独立折叠、执行特定功能的紧凑部分
senses.example: The kinase domain binds the phosphate donor.
senses.exampleCN: 激酶结构域结合磷酸供体。
senses.why: Structural biology borrowed the word for a self-governing part: a domain folds on its own and can be moved between proteins, like a small territory with its own rule.
senses.whyCN: 结构生物学借用这个词来指一个自治的部分：结构域自行折叠，还能在蛋白质之间搬移，像一片自有规则的小领地。

senses.title: A security or administrative domain in computing
senses.titleCN: 计算机中的安全域或管理域
senses.definition: a bounded area of a network or system governed by one set of access rules
senses.definitionCN: 由一套访问规则管辖的网络或系统区域
senses.example: No account may cross from one domain to another without a new login.
senses.exampleCN: 没有新的登录，任何账户都不得从一个域越到另一个域。
senses.why: Computing reused the political model directly: one administrator, one rule set, one boundary that traffic must not cross freely.
senses.whyCN: 计算机直接沿用这个政治模型：一个管理员、一套规则、一条流量不得随意越过的边界。

senses.title: The domain of discourse in logic
senses.definition: the set of individuals over which a quantifier ranges in a logical statement
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑陈述中量词所涵盖的个体集合
senses.example: The sentence is true only within the domain of discourse specified.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话只在所指定的论域内为真。
senses.why: Logic needed a name for the range a statement speaks about, and the domain supplied it: whatever falls outside is simply not being discussed.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要为陈述所谈的范围取一个名称，domain 提供了它：落在范围之外的东西，根本没有被讨论。

intro.en: Domain comes from Latin dominium 'ownership, lordship', built on dominus 'master' and domus 'house'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domain 来自拉丁 dominium「所有权、主权」，由 dominus「主人」与 domus「房屋」构成，经法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Domus meant 'house, household'. It is the oldest layer: a domain begins as the house a master rules.
items.cn: domus 意为「房屋、家户」。它是最古老的一层：领地最初就是主人所治的家宅。

items.en: Dominus meant 'master, lord', from domus; it produced dominate, dominion and dominus in ecclesiastical use.
items.cn: dominus 意为「主人、领主」，出自 domus；它产生 dominate、dominion，并在教会用语中保留 dominus。

items.en: Dominium meant 'ownership, property, sovereignty', and Medieval Latin extended it to a lord's land.
items.cn: dominium 意为「所有权、财产、主权」，中世纪拉丁语把它扩展到领主的土地。

items.en: Old French domaine brought the word into English with the sense of a lord's estate, later widened to any sphere.
items.cn: 古法语 domaine 把该词带入英语，义为领主的产业，后扩展到任何范围。

items.en: Mathematics, computing and biology each borrowed the word for a bounded area of authority; Woese's three-domain classification then placed domain above kingdom, giving the old word its highest taxonomic rank.
items.cn: 数学、计算机与生物学各自借用这个词来指有边界的权辖范围；沃斯的三域分类随后把 domain 置于界之上，使这个旧词获得最高的分类阶元位置。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of domain is not fixed here; the link of dominus to domus is generally accepted but the pre-Latin origin of domus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：domain 最早的英语使用此处无法确定；dominus 与 domus 的联系一般认为是成立的，但 domus 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the Latin domus/dominus stock; group two compares spheres, ranks and territories.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁 domus／dominus 词干的词；第二组比较范围、阶元与领土。

entries.definition: To control or tower over, from dominari 'to rule'. It names the act of holding a domain.
entries.definitionCN: 支配或高耸于，来自 dominari「统治」。它指持有领域的动作。

entries.definition: Sovereignty or a ruled territory, from dominium. It is the political twin of domain.
entries.definitionCN: 主权或被统治的领土，来自 dominium。它是 domain 的政治同义词。

entries.definition: A small tile used in a game, from dominus by way of the phrase 'lord' used in old game calls; unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 游戏用的小牌，经旧时游戏呼语中的「主人」一词来自 dominus；意义上无关。

entries.definition: A lord's own land kept for his use, from dominicum. It is the concrete estate behind the abstract domain.
entries.definitionCN: 领主保留自用的土地，出自 dominicum。它是抽象 domain 背后的具体产业。

entries.definition: A branch of study or an area of practical activity. It is looser than domain and implies no boundary or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 一个研究分支或实践领域。比 domain 宽松，不含边界或权威之意。

entries.definition: The taxonomic rank below domain in the three-domain scheme; each domain contains several kingdoms.
entries.definitionCN: 三域方案中域之下的阶元；每个域包含若干界。

entries.definition: A kingdom or an area of activity, used more in writing than in technical prose.
entries.definitionCN: 王国或活动领域，较多用于写作而非技术文献。

entries.definition: A defined area, often one defended by an animal or claimed by a state; it stresses space more than authority.
entries.definitionCN: 被界定的区域，常由动物防卫或由国家主张；比 domain 更强调空间而非权威。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dominus 'master' + domus 'house': a domain is where a master's word runs.
normal.cn: dominus「主人」+ domus「房屋」：领域就是主人的话得以施行之处。

normal.en: The technical senses all keep a boundary: a function's inputs, a network's rules, a protein's folded part.
normal.cn: 各技术义都保留一条边界：函数的输入、网络的规则、蛋白质的折叠部分。

normal.en: In the three-domain scheme, domain is now the highest rank, above kingdom.
normal.cn: 在三域方案中，域是最高阶元，位于界之上。

normal.en: A domain name is the corner of the network its holder governs.
normal.cn: 域名就是持有者所管辖的网络角落。

normal.en: Eminent domain is the state's ultimate lordship over land.
normal.cn: 国家征用权是国家对土地的终极领主权。

examples.en: The question lies outside my domain, so I sent it to a colleague.
examples.cn: 这个问题超出我的领域，所以我转给了同事。

examples.en: Archaea were given their own domain on the basis of ribosomal sequences.
examples.cn: 古菌依据核糖体序列被给予自己的一个域。

examples.en: The domain name was transferred without changing the site.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「do 做 + main 主要」——主要归我做的那片范围 → domain 领域；域

root: 拉丁 dominium「所有权、主权」，由 dominus「主人」与 domus「房屋」构成；经法语 domaine 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of domain all describe a bounded area under one authority: a scholar's field, the highest taxonomic rank, an internet address, a function's inputs, state taking power, a lord's land, a folded protein part, a network's rule zone and a logical universe of discourse.
sensesIntro.cn: domain 的九个义项都描述一片在一个权属之下、有边界的范围：学者的领域、最高分类阶元、互联网地址、函数的输入、国家征用权、领主的土地、蛋白质折叠部分、网络的规则区域，以及逻辑论域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bounded area where one rule runs, marked at the threshold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片有边界、由一条规则统辖的区域，门槛上划着界线。

branches.en: THE OLD CORE: a master's house and a lord's land are the concrete origin of every later sense.
branches.cn: 古老核心：主人的家宅与领主的土地，是其后各义的具体源头。

branches.en: THE WIDEST AND THE FORMAL: biology's top rank and logic's universe of discourse are both total ranges.
branches.cn: 最宽与最形式化：生物学的最高阶元与逻辑学的论域都是总体范围。

branches.en: RULED CORNERS: a domain name and a security domain are network territory with one administrator.
branches.cn: 被管辖的角落：域名与安全域都是有一个管理者的网络领土。

branches.en: SELF-GOVERNING PARTS: a function acts only on its domain, and a protein domain folds on its own.
branches.cn: 自治的部分：函数只在定义域内起作用，蛋白质结构域自行折叠。

branches.en: THE ULTIMATE CLAIM: eminent domain is the state's lordship overriding a private owner.
branches.cn: 终极主张：国家征用权是国家领主权压过私人所有者。

intro.en: Domain is one Latin word for lordship that has been borrowed by every discipline that needs a bounded area of authority.
intro.cn: domain 是一个表示领主权的拉丁词，被每一个需要有界权辖范围的学科借用。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus and dominus give domain, dominate, dominant, dominion, domino and demesne; dominium is the direct source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 domus 与 dominus 给出 domain、dominate、dominant、dominion、domino、demesne；dominium 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: The house is the oldest image of a domain.
items.exampleCN: 家宅是领域最古老的意象。

items.example: Dominus supplies the authority in the word.
items.exampleCN: dominus 提供这个词中的权威。

items.example: Dominium is the direct source of domain.
items.exampleCN: dominium 是 domain 的直接来源。

items.example: A domain has a threshold and a rule.
items.exampleCN: 一个领域有门槛，也有规则。

items.example: To dominate is to hold a domain over others.
items.exampleCN: 支配就是对人持有领域。

items.example: Dominion is the political twin of domain.
items.exampleCN: dominion 是 domain 的政治同义词。

items.example: The demesne is the concrete estate.
Domino shares the root but not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: domino 共用词根，却不共用意义。

items.example: Kingdom now sits below domain.

definition_zh: 穹顶；圆顶；半球形顶盖；穹丘；（俚语）头顶
definition_en: a rounded roof shaped like half a ball, or any object with such a top
core_image: 一圈圆形石墙向上收拢，最后在正中合成一个采光的小孔
scene: 圆形大厅的墙向上收拢，顶部只留一个采光孔。The dome above the hall carries the weight of the whole roof without a single interior column.
sceneCN: 这里 dome 指「半球形的圆顶屋顶」（第 1 个义项：穹顶）；句意为大厅上方的穹顶不用一根内柱就承起整片屋顶。图中可辨识物件：圆形石墙、采光孔、大厅地面、屋顶轮廓。

pos.zh: 穹顶；圆顶；圆顶建筑；穹状顶盖；穹丘

senses.title: A rounded roof
senses.definition: a roof formed as a hemisphere or similar curved surface over a circular or polygonal space
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖圆形或多边形空间的半球形或类似曲面屋顶
senses.example: The dome rests on a ring of stone called a drum.
senses.exampleCN: 穹顶架在一圈称为鼓座的石环上。
senses.why: the shape is the sense: a curved surface that closes a round space without internal supports.
senses.whyCN: 形状就是词义：一种不用内部支撑就能封住圆形空间的曲面。

senses.title: A domed building
senses.definition: a building whose most prominent feature is its dome, such as a capitol or an observatory
senses.definitionCN: 以穹顶为最显著特征的建筑，如议会大厦或天文台
senses.example: The observatory dome rotates to follow the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 天文台的圆顶会转动以追随天空。
senses.why: by metonymy the roof stands for the whole building, especially when the roof is what people recognize.
senses.whyCN: 以提喻法，屋顶代表整座建筑，尤其当人们认出的正是那片屋顶时。

senses.title: Any hemispherical cover
senses.definition: a rounded cover on an object, such as a tank, a lamp or a stadium roof
senses.definitionCN: 物体上的圆顶盖，如储罐、灯具或体育场屋顶
senses.example: The fuel tank's dome vents gas when pressure rises.
senses.exampleCN: 压力升高时，燃料罐的圆顶会排气。
senses.why: the architectural shape is abstracted into any rounded lid or cap.
senses.whyCN: 建筑形状被抽象成任何圆形的盖或罩。

senses.title: A geological dome
senses.definition: a rounded uplift of rock or salt, often formed by pressure from below
senses.definitionCN: 由下方压力形成的岩石或盐层圆形隆起
senses.example: The salt dome traps oil in the layers above it.
senses.exampleCN: 盐穹把石油封存在其上方的岩层里。
senses.why: geology borrowed the shape word because a rising mass of salt or lava looks like a roof from below.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用了这个形状词，因为上升的盐体或熔岩从下方看就像一片屋顶。

senses.title: A slang word for the head
senses.definition: in informal use, the top of a person's head
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指人的头顶
senses.example: He took off his cap and rubbed his dome.
senses.exampleCN: 他摘下帽子，摸了摸脑袋。
senses.why: the slang keeps only the roundness and position of a dome, with no architecture left.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语只保留了穹顶的圆与位置，建筑义已不剩。

senses.title: The vault of the sky
senses.definition: the sky pictured as a great curved roof over the earth
senses.definitionCN: 把天空想象成覆盖大地的巨大曲面屋顶
senses.example: Stars filled the dome of heaven above the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 星空布满沙漠上方的天穹。
senses.why: ancient cosmology pictured the sky as a solid bowl, and the image survives in poetry.
senses.whyCN: 古代宇宙观把天空想象成一只实心碗，这个意象在诗歌中留存。

senses.title: A domed sports arena
senses.definition: a large indoor arena whose roof is a dome, often referred to by the name Dome
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶为穹形的大型室内场馆，常直接以「圆顶」为名
senses.example: The finals were played under the dome before sixty thousand people.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛在这座圆顶场馆内、六万人面前举行。
senses.why: venues took the building part as a brand, so the word now names arenas as well as roofs.
senses.whyCN: 场馆把这一建筑部件当作招牌，因此这个词也指场馆本身。

senses.title: A cathedral in Italian usage
senses.titleCN: 意大利语中的主教座堂
senses.definition: the older English sense, from Italian, of a cathedral church, especially one with a dome
senses.definitionCN: 英语旧义，来自意大利语，指主教座堂，尤指带穹顶者
senses.example: The guide calls the cathedral simply the dome, as Italians do.
senses.exampleCN: 导游像意大利人那样，径直把这座主教座堂称作圆顶。
senses.why: the English word entered through the Italian name for a cathedral, so the building and its roof were once the same word.
senses.whyCN: 英语词是经意大利语中「主教座堂」之名进来的，因此建筑与屋顶曾同为一词。

intro.en: Dome entered English through French from the Italian word for a cathedral, and only later narrowed to the rounded roof. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dome 经法语从意大利语中「主教座堂」一词进入英语，后来才收窄为圆形屋顶。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus meant house or household, and the phrase for a house of God supplied the Italian church word.
items.cn: domus 意为房屋或家庭，「上帝之屋」这一短语给出了意大利语的教堂词。

items.en: Duomo named a cathedral, especially the principal church of a city, and many such churches carried a dome.
items.cn: duomo 指主教座堂，尤指一座城市的主要教堂，而许多此类教堂都带穹顶。

items.en: French dôme borrowed the Italian word and used it for the rounded roof as well as the church.
items.cn: 法语 dôme 借入意大利语词，既用于教堂，也用于圆形屋顶。

items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century, when domes were being built again in Britain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该词，其时英国正重新兴建穹顶。

items.en: In later centuries geology and engineering applied the shape word to salt uplifts, tank tops and stadium roofs.
items.cn: 在后来的世纪里，地质与工程把这个形状词用于盐层隆起、罐顶与体育场屋顶。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of domus is not settled, and the Indo-European root usually cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：domus 在拉丁语之前的谱系尚无定论，通常为其引用的印欧语词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds curved-roof words that are often confused; group two holds words for rounded tops and for the buildings beneath them.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的曲面屋顶词；第二组是圆顶状顶盖与穹顶之下建筑的词。

entries.definition: A small dome-like structure on a roof, often with windows; it sits on the roof rather than covering the whole room.
entries.definitionCN: 屋顶上的小型穹状结构，常带窗；它置于屋顶之上，而非覆盖整个房间。

entries.definition: The Italian word for a cathedral, which gave dome its English sense; it names the church, not the roof.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语中「主教座堂」一词，给了 dome 英语词义；它指教堂，而非屋顶。

entries.definition: Having a dome; it describes a building or object rather than naming the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 有圆顶的；描述建筑或物体，而非命名结构。

entries.definition: Of dome form, used in architectural writing; it never names a physical dome.
entries.definitionCN: 穹顶形式的，用于建筑写作；从不指实体穹顶。

entries.definition: An arched ceiling, usually continuous along a corridor; a dome is a vault turned around a central point.
entries.definitionCN: 拱形顶棚，通常沿走廊连续延伸；穹顶是绕中心点旋转的拱顶。

entries.definition: A curved structure spanning an opening; a dome is a curved roof, while an arch is a curved span.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越开口的曲线结构；穹顶是曲面屋顶，拱则是曲线跨度。

entries.definition: A tall pointed structure on a tower; it rises to a point, while a dome closes in a curve.
entries.definitionCN: 塔上高耸的尖顶；它收成一点，而穹顶以曲线闭合。

entries.definition: The covering of a building; a dome is one kind of roof with a particular geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的覆盖物；穹顶是其中一种具有特定几何形状的屋顶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Italian route, the real shape words and the real technical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的意大利语来源路径、真实的形状词与真实的技术复合词。

normal.en: The word travelled from 'house of God' to 'cathedral' to 'rounded roof'.
normal.cn: 这个词从「上帝之屋」走到「主教座堂」，再到「圆形屋顶」。

normal.en: The family runs dome, domed, domical, semi-dome, dome-shaped, doming.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dome、domed、domical、semi-dome、dome-shaped、doming。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: glass dome, salt dome, lava dome, dome of heaven.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：玻璃圆顶、盐穹、熔岩穹丘、天穹。

normal.en: A dome closes a round space without interior columns; that is its engineering point.
normal.cn: 穹顶不用内柱就能封住圆形空间，这正是它的工程要点。

normal.en: The slang sense keeps only the round top of a head.
normal.cn: 俚语义只保留了脑袋的圆顶。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl turned upside down and made of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倒扣过来的碗，材料是石头。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the ceiling is the sky and the walls are only a rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一间以天空为顶、墙只剩一圈边缘的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium breathing under a single continuous lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场在一整片连续的盖下呼吸。

examples.en: The dome was regilded after a century of weather.
examples.cn: 经历一个世纪的风雨之后，穹顶被重新贴金。

examples.en: A glass dome covers the whole courtyard.
examples.cn: 一座玻璃圆顶覆盖整个庭院。

examples.en: Drilling stopped when the bit reached the salt dome.
examples.cn: 钻头抵达盐穹时，钻探停止了。

dict_mnemonic.text: duomo（主教座堂）→ 教堂上的圆屋顶 → 穹顶；也指任何圆顶盖

root: 法语 dôme 来自意大利 duomo「主教座堂」，其源头是拉丁 domus「房屋、家」，尤指「上帝之屋」；英语 dome 由教堂义转为圆顶义。domus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one curve: a roof closes a round room, then stands for a building, a lid, a rock uplift, a head, the sky, an arena and an old name for a cathedral.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条曲线展开：屋顶封住圆形房间，再代表整座建筑、一只盖、一处岩隆、一个头、一片天、一座场馆，以及主教座堂的旧称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of wall rising and closing into one point of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈墙向上升起，最后收拢成一点光。

branches.en: THE ROOF: the first sense is the curved surface that closes a round space.
branches.cn: 屋顶：第一个义项是封住圆形空间的曲面。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: an observatory and an arena are known by the roof that crowns them.
branches.cn: 建筑：天文台与体育馆都因冠于其上的屋顶而被认出。

branches.en: THE SHAPE ITSELF: a tank lid and a salt uplift are the same curve at different scales.
branches.cn: 形状本身：罐盖与盐穹，是同一曲线的不同尺度。

branches.en: ROUND TOPS: a head and the sky repeat the dome as a plain image of roundness.
branches.cn: 圆顶：脑袋与天空把穹顶重复为单纯的圆形意象。

branches.en: THE OLD NAME: Italian usage once made the cathedral and its roof a single word.
branches.cn: 旧名：意大利语用法曾让主教座堂与其屋顶同为一词。

intro.en: Dome has no productive prefix or suffix in English; its history is a borrowing from a house word to a roof word, and its derived forms simply add English endings.
intro.cn: dome 在英语中没有能产的前缀或后缀；它的历史是从「房屋」词借为「屋顶」词，其派生形式只是加英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus is the ultimate source, through Italian duomo and French dôme; Latin also had the adjective domesticus from the same house word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus 是最终源头，经意大利语 duomo 与法语 dôme 而来；拉丁语还有同出「房屋」词的形容词 domesticus。

items.example: Domus named a home before it named a church.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先指家，后指教堂。

items.example: The duomo stands in the centre of the old city.
items.exampleCN: 主教座堂立在老城中心。

items.example: French kept both meanings for a time.
items.exampleCN: 法语有一段时间两义并用。

items.example: The dome covers the crossing.
A domed hall reflects sound for seconds.
items.exampleCN: 带穹顶的大厅能把声音反射数秒。

items.example: The domical vault is a technical label.
items.exampleCN: 穹形拱顶是一个技术标签。

items.meaning: a half dome, as over an apse
items.meaningCN: 半穹顶，如后殿上方的顶
items.example: A semi-dome closes the apse.

items.meaning: having the form of a dome
items.example: A dome-shaped lid seals the tank.

definition_zh: 家庭的；家务的；国内的；驯养的
definition_en: relating to the home or family, to one's own country, or to animals kept by people
core_image: 厨房窗台上晾着洗好的碗，楼下传来自家孩子的脚步声
scene: 周末早晨厨房里飘着面包香，孩子还在客厅搭积木。Domestic chores fall to her on Sundays.
sceneCN: 这里 domestic 是「家庭的、家务的」（第 1 个义项：与家庭和家务有关）；句意是星期天大部分家务都落在她身上。

pos.zh: 家庭的；家务的；国内的；驯养的
家仆（旧用法，多用于英式英语）

derivatives.zh: 已驯化的；习惯家庭生活的

senses.title: Of the home and household
senses.definition: relating to the home, the household or family life
senses.definitionCN: 与家、家庭生活或家务有关的
senses.example: They argued about how to share domestic work.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为如何分担家务争吵过。
senses.why: Latin domus meant house, so the adjective begins as a word about everything inside the walls of a home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 domus 是「房子」，所以这个形容词一开始就指家门以内的一切。

senses.title: Within one country
senses.definition: relating to one's own country rather than to foreign countries
senses.definitionCN: 与本国内部有关，而非与外国有关的
senses.example: Domestic flights leave from the older terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 国内航班从较旧的航站楼出发。
senses.why: A country is imagined as a large household, so affairs inside its borders are domestic affairs.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家被想象成一个大家庭，因此国境之内的事务就是「家里的」事务。

senses.title: Tamed, not wild
senses.definition: kept by people as a pet or farm animal rather than living in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养作宠物或农用，而非野生生活的
senses.example: The farm keeps both domestic and wild species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场既养家养品种，也养野生物种。
senses.why: An animal brought into the house or the yard has crossed the same boundary as a household matter.
senses.whyCN: 被带进屋里或院里的动物，和家务事一样跨过了「家门」这条界线。

intro.en: Domestic comes from Latin domesticus, belonging to the house, and the root domus, house.
intro.cn: domestic 来自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），其根是 domus（房子）。

items.en: The root behind domus is generally reconstructed as a word for house or household; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: domus 背后的词根一般重构为表示「房子、家户」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Domus meant a house or a household, and it produced dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，它还生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domesticus meant belonging to the household, and it was also used for household servants.
items.cn: domesticus 表示「属于家户的」，也用来指家仆。

items.en: Old French domestique passed the adjective into English with both the home and the servant senses.
items.cn: 古法语 domestique 把这个形容词带入英语，家庭义与家仆义一并传入。

items.en: English extended the word from the household to the nation, speaking of domestic affairs.
items.cn: 英语把它从家户扩展到国家，开始说 domestic affairs（国内事务）。

items.en: The adjective now covers chores, flights, animals and products of a whole country.
items.cn: 今天这个形容词覆盖家务、航班、动物，以及一国的产品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin domus root; the near-meaning group gathers household and internal words.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 domus 词根；近义组收的是家庭与「内部」类的词。

entries.definition: To tame an animal or bring it into human use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驯化、使家养」，由本词加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: The quality or state of home life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家庭生活、恋家」，同出 domus。

entries.definition: A person's permanent home, from Latin domicilium; it shares domus but has a different spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所」，来自拉丁语 domicilium；与 domestic 同出 domus，但拼写路径不同。

entries.definition: All the people living together in one home; often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「家户、家庭的」，指同住一屋的人。

entries.definition: Inside a country or organisation; the usual word in political contexts for domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，在政治语境中常与 domestic 对应。

entries.definition: An animal that is no longer wild; narrower than domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「驯服的」，范围比 domestic 的驯养义更窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real domus family from the house to the nation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 domus 词族，从房子一直走到国家。

normal.en: Domus is house; domesticus is what belongs to the house.
normal.cn: domus 是房子，domesticus 就是属于这座房子的。

normal.en: Dominus, master of the house, comes from the same domus.
normal.cn: dominus 意为一家之主，也出自同一个 domus。

normal.en: A domestic flight stays inside the country, as if the nation were one house.
normal.cn: 国内航班留在国境之内，仿佛整个国家是一间大房子。

normal.en: Domestic animals have been brought into the human household.
normal.cn: 家养动物已经被带进了人类的家庭。

normal.en: Gross domestic product counts what is produced inside those borders.
normal.cn: 国内生产总值算的是这些边界之内生产的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a warm kitchen seen from the street, with one lamp still on.
abstract.cn: 想象从街上望见一间温暖的厨房，还亮着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a map of one country drawn as a single house.
abstract.cn: 想象把一国的地图画成一间房子。

abstract.en: Picture a fence where wild grass stops and a swept yard begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，外面是野草，里面是扫干净的院子。

examples.en: Domestic work should not fall on one person alone.
examples.cn: 家务不应只落在一个人身上。

examples.en: The airline added two new domestic routes.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司新增了两条国内航线。

examples.en: Domestic cats sleep far more than their wild cousins.
examples.cn: 家猫比野外的同类睡得多得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: dom 有「家、屋」的意思，-estic 是形容词后缀：属于这间屋子的，就是家庭的、国内的。

root: 源自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），由 domus（房子、家户）加形容词后缀 -icus 构成；domus 同时生出 dominus（一家之主）。古法语 domestique 把家庭义与家仆义传入英语，十六世纪起从家户扩展指国家内部。

sensesIntro.en: One root imagines a house, then stretches it to a nation and to animals brought indoors.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根先想象一间房子，再把它拉到整个国家，以及被带进屋里的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kitchen seen from the street, warm inside and swept clean.
core.cn: 核心意象：从街上望见的一间厨房，里面温暖，地面扫得干净。

branches.en: THE HOME: the first sense covers everything inside the walls of a house.
branches.cn: 家庭线：第一个义项覆盖家门以内的一切。

branches.en: THE NATION: a country is treated as a large household, so inside affairs are domestic.
branches.cn: 国家线：国家被当作大家庭，因此境内事务称作 domestic。

branches.en: THE YARD: tame animals have crossed the same boundary into human keeping.
branches.cn: 院子线：驯养动物跨过同一条界线，进入人的照料范围。

branches.en: House and country share the word because both are spaces one belongs to.
branches.cn: 家庭与国家共用一个词，因为两者都是人所属的空间。

branches.en: A domestic animal is simply a creature moved into the household.
branches.cn: 家养动物不过是被移进家户的一种生物。

intro.en: Domestic joins the Latin house root domus to the adjective suffix -icus, which English keeps as -ic.
intro.cn: domestic 把拉丁语「房子」词根 domus 接到形容词后缀 -icus 上，英语保留为 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, domesticus and dominus are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、domesticus 与 dominus 均有记录，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: The noun is the house at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是这一族词的中心「房子」。

items.example: The adjective already carried the home sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词已带有家庭义。

items.example: It forms domestic.
People domesticated wheat long ago.
items.exampleCN: 人类很久以前就驯化了小麦。

items.example: Domestication changed the dog's body.
He missed the domesticity of his parents' house.
items.exampleCN: 他想念父母家中的家庭生活。

items.example: Her domicile is listed on the form.
It forms domesticity.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「驯化；使适应家庭生活」
由 domesticate 加 -ion 构成，义为「驯化；归化」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「家庭生活；恋家」

definition_zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培；使适应家庭生活；使（条约）转为国内法
definition_en: to bring a wild animal or plant under human control and use
core_image: 一双手把一只挣扎的幼兽按在膝上，另一只手把门闩轻轻扣上
scene: 农人把野生的禾草一株株挑出来留种，Farmers domesticate the wild grass by saving seed from the calmest plants.
sceneCN: 这里 domesticate 指「把野生植物选育为栽培作物」（第 2 个义项：栽培化）；句意为农人从最安静的植株上留种，从而驯化这种野草。图中可辨识物件：留种穗、麻袋、挑选的手、田垄。

pos.zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培；使适应家庭生活
（罕用）已驯化的动物

senses.title: Tame an animal over generations
senses.definition: to breed and manage a wild animal population so that it lives under human care
senses.definitionCN: 繁育并管理野生兽群，使其生活在人类照料之下
senses.example: People domesticated dogs long before they kept herds.
senses.exampleCN: 人们养畜群之前很久就驯化了狗。
senses.why: the verb is the act behind domestication, and its object is a population rather than a single pet.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是驯化背后的动作，其对象是一个群体，而不是一只宠物。

senses.title: Turn a wild plant into a crop
senses.definition: to select and cultivate a wild plant until it depends on human sowing
senses.definitionCN: 对野生植物进行选育与栽培，直到它依赖人播种
senses.example: Early farmers domesticated barley without knowing genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 早期农民不懂遗传学，却驯化了二棱大麦。
senses.why: the plant sense repeats the animal sense at the level of seed rather than behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 植物义在种子层面重复了动物义，而不是在行为层面。

senses.title: Adapt a species genetically
senses.definition: to bring about inherited changes that suit a species to human environments
senses.definitionCN: 造成可遗传的改变，使某物种适应人类环境
senses.example: Selective breeding domesticated the temperament as well as the body.
senses.exampleCN: 选育既驯化了身体，也驯化了性情。
senses.why: when the change is heritable, taming one generation domesticates the line.
senses.whyCN: 当改变可遗传时，驯服一代就驯化了整条线。

senses.title: Accustom a person to home life
senses.definition: to make a person used to the routines and confines of a household
senses.definitionCN: 使人习惯于家户的日常与范围
senses.example: Years of indoor work had domesticated him more than he admitted.
senses.exampleCN: 多年室内工作使他安于家居，比他承认的更甚。
senses.why: the household image turns on a person, and the verb now means settling someone into domestic routine.
senses.whyCN: 家户意象转向人，动词于是指让人安于家庭日常。

senses.title: Make something familiar and manageable
senses.definition: to make an unfamiliar idea, tool or practice easy to live with
senses.definitionCN: 使陌生的想法、工具或做法易于共处
senses.example: The handbook domesticated a difficult theory for new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册把一套艰深理论变得新员工也能上手。
senses.why: anything wild or intimidating can be brought indoors metaphorically.
senses.whyCN: 任何野生或令人畏惧之物，都可以在比喻意义上被带进屋内。

senses.title: Incorporate a treaty into domestic law
senses.definition: in law, to give an international agreement effect within a national legal order
senses.definitionCN: 法律上使国际协定在国内法律秩序中生效
senses.example: Parliament domesticated the convention by statute.
senses.exampleCN: 议会以法规把该公约转为国内法。
senses.why: the international text must be brought into the house of national law before courts can apply it.
senses.whyCN: 国际文本必须先被带进国家法律这座房子，法院才能适用。

senses.title: A domesticated animal, as a rare noun
senses.titleCN: 作为罕用名词的驯化动物
senses.definition: rarely, a domesticated animal or plant considered as an entity
senses.definitionCN: 罕用，指作为实体的已驯化动植物
senses.example: The farm keeps four domesticates and a dozen wild species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养四种驯化种和十几种野生种。
senses.why: English often lets a verb form double as a noun, and specialists use it for the organism itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让动词形式兼作名词，专业人士用它指生物本身。

senses.title: Settle and work a landscape
senses.definition: to bring land into settled, managed use
senses.definitionCN: 把土地纳入定居、有管理的使用
senses.example: The valley was domesticated by terrace builders a thousand years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷在一千年前被修梯田的人驯化了。
senses.why: if a species can be brought into the household, so can the ground it grows on.
senses.whyCN: 既然物种能被带进家户，它生长的土地也可以。

intro.en: Domesticate comes from Latin domesticare 'to make domestic', built on domesticus 'of the household'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domesticate 出自拉丁 domesticare「使家用、使驯服」，建于 domesticus「属于家户的」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus 'house' is the base of the family. Its deeper origin is reconstructed, and the common link to a building root remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: domus「房子」是整个词族的基础。其更深来源属重构，通常联系的「建造」词根仍是假说。

items.en: Domesticus described what belongs to a household, including animals kept indoors.
items.cn: domesticus 描述属于家户之物，包括养在屋内的动物。

items.en: Domesticare meant 'to make domestic, to tame'; it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: domesticare 意为「使家用、使驯服」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English domesticate is recorded in the seventeenth century, at first for animals and later for plants.
items.cn: 英语 domesticate 在 17 世纪有记录，先用于动物，后用于植物。

items.en: The verb was extended to people, tools and treaties; the legal use is recent and its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词后来扩展到人、工具与条约；法律用法较晚，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin household family; the second lists other verbs of bringing something under control.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁「家户」词族；第二组是把某物置于控制之下的其他动词。

entries.definition: Of the home or of animals kept there; an adjective, where domesticate is the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭的或家养的；是形容词，domesticate 是动作。

entries.definition: Already tamed or adapted; it reports a result, while domesticate names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被驯化或适应；报告结果，而 domesticate 指做的动作。

entries.definition: The whole historical process; the verb can be one step inside that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个历史过程；动词可以是这个过程里的一步。

entries.definition: The state or quality of home life; it has no taming sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭生活的状态或性质；完全没有驯化含义。

entries.definition: To make one animal calm around people; it need not change the species or its offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 使单只动物在人前安静；不必改变物种或后代。

entries.definition: To prepare and tend land or plants; the labour can occur without any inherited change.
entries.definitionCN: 整地并照料土地或植物；这种劳动可以没有可遗传的改变。

entries.definition: To mate selected animals or plants; it is the mechanism often used to domesticate.
entries.definitionCN: 让选定的动植物交配；常是驯化所用的机制。

entries.definition: To establish a species in a new region; the aim is survival there, not human use.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物种在新地区立足；目标是当地存活，而非人类利用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin house verb, the regular English endings and the objects the verb takes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「房子」动词、规则的英语词尾，以及这个动词常带的宾语。

normal.en: domesticus 'of the house' + -are 'to make' = to make something house-broken.
normal.cn: domesticus「属于房子」+ -are「使」= 使某物适应屋内生活。

normal.en: The verb is regular: domesticates, domesticated, domesticated, domesticating.
normal.cn: 这个动词规则变化：domesticates、domesticated、domesticated、domesticating。

normal.en: Typical objects are animals, plants, species and treaties.
normal.cn: 典型宾语是动物、植物、物种与条约。

normal.en: The result adjective is domesticated, and the process noun is domestication.
normal.cn: 结果形容词是 domesticated，过程名词是 domestication。

normal.en: Domare 'to tame' looks related in meaning but is a separate Latin verb.
normal.cn: domare「使驯服」在意义上看似相关，却是另一个拉丁动词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing gently on a young animal until it stops struggling.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻按在幼兽身上，直到它不再挣扎。

abstract.en: Picture a door latch that can be opened from inside but not from outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一把门闩，从里面能开，从外面打不开。

abstract.en: Picture a wild field being taught to hold still in rows.
abstract.cn: 想象一片野地被教着站成一排排。

examples.en: Farmers domesticated rice in several river valleys independently.
examples.cn: 农民在几处河谷各自独立地驯化了水稻。

examples.en: You cannot domesticate a species in one lifetime.
examples.cn: 一个物种不可能在一代人的时间里被驯化。

examples.en: The state domesticated the agreement through a new act.
examples.cn: 该国以一部新法把该协定转为国内法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多麦斯提凯特」听成「多把麦子提进家」——野物提进家门，喂熟、留种，就是驯化。

root: 拉丁 domus「房子、家户」→ domesticus「属于家户的」→ domesticare「使家用、使驯服」，英语直接借其动词形作 domesticate。domare「使驯服」为另一动词，不与此同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from taming animals and plants through genetic adaptation, human domestication, familiarising ideas, legal incorporation, the rare noun and settled land.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从驯养动植物，经遗传适应、人的家居化、想法日常化、法律纳入、罕用名词，到土地的定居经营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a young animal while the gate is latched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住幼兽，另一只手扣上门闩。

branches.en: BEAST AND CROP: behaviour and seed are two handles on the same act of bringing inside.
branches.cn: 兽与作物：行为与种子，是把同一「带进家户」动作的两个抓手。

branches.en: THE LINE AND THE THING: inherited change makes a lineage domestic, and the resulting organism can be counted.
branches.cn: 谱系与个体：可遗传的改变使一条谱系家养化，其结果生物也就可以计数。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a human can be settled into a household as surely as an animal.
branches.cn: 人：人也可以像动物一样被安顿进家户。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a difficult theory is brought indoors until ordinary people can live with it.
branches.cn: 想法：艰深理论被带进屋内，直到普通人能与它共处。

branches.en: LAW AND GROUND: a treaty enters national law, and a valley enters settled use.
branches.cn: 法律与土地：条约进入国家法，山谷进入定居使用。

intro.en: Domesticate is a Latin household adjective plus a Latin verb ending, with English tense endings added on top.
intro.cn: domesticate 是拉丁「家户」形容词加拉丁动词词尾，其上又加英语时态词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus gives domicile, domestic and domesticate; the taming verb domare is a different root and should not be folded in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 domus 给出 domicile、domestic、domesticate；表驯服的 domare 属另一词根，不应并入。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「屋内」的意思。

items.example: The ending makes a verb of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把形容词变成动词。

items.example: They domesticated the local grain.
items.exampleCN: 他们驯化了当地的谷物。

items.exampleCN: 驯化改变了该地区的饮食。

items.example: Domestic life settled around the hearth.
items.exampleCN: 家庭生活围绕炉灶展开。

items.example: The tax domicile is the family house.

definition_en: the state of being dominant: control over others, the position of greatest power or importance, and the corresponding technical states in ecology, genetics, markets, and behaviour
core_image: 高山俯瞰周围的丘陵，所有视线都要向上仰望它
scene: 一座主峰高过四周丘陵，谷里每条小路都通向它的阴影。One peak rises above the surrounding hills, and every trail in the valley leads toward its shadow. That peak holds its dominance over the whole valley.
sceneCN: 这里 dominance 是「优势、支配地位」（第 2 个义项：最重要、最强势的地位）；句意：一座山峰高过周围丘陵，对整条山谷占据支配地位，谷中每条小路都通向它的阴影。图中可辨识物件：主峰、较低的丘陵、放射状的小径、山脚的村落、峰顶的旗帜。

pos.zh: 支配地位；优势；控制；生态优势度；显性

collocations.zh: 支配等级（动物群体中的位次序列）
某物种在群落中的优势度

forms.label: 复数（多种优势状态，较少用）

senses.title: Control over others: making another obey
senses.titleCN: 对他人的控制：使对方服从
senses.definition: the exercise of power or influence over other people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 对其他人或群体施加权力或影响力
senses.example: The party's dominance over local politics lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 该党对地方政治的支配持续了四十年。
senses.why: Dominance is dominant plus -ance, and dominant is Latin dominantem, the present participle of dominari 'to rule'. The noun names the ongoing state of ruling rather than one act of conquest.
senses.whyCN: dominance 是 dominant 加 -ance，而 dominant 是拉丁语 dominantem——dominari“统治”的现在分词。这个名词指持续的统治状态，而非一次征服行为。

senses.title: Top position: being the most important or strongest
senses.titleCN: 最上位：最重要、最强势的地位
senses.definition: the position of greatest prominence, strength, or importance in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域中地位最显著、力量最强或最重要
senses.example: English retains its dominance as the language of scientific publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 英语仍保持作为科学出版语言的支配地位。
senses.why: The image behind dominus, 'master of a house', is spatial: one point stands above the rest. Applied to a field, dominance is that top point, whether or not anyone literally obeys.
senses.whyCN: dominus“一家之主”背后的意象是空间性的：一个点高过其余。用于某个领域时，dominance 就是这个最高的点，无论有没有人真的服从。

senses.title: Ecological dominance: one species outweighs the rest
senses.titleCN: 生态优势：一个物种在群落中占压倒地位
senses.definition: the condition in which one species controls a community's structure through numbers or size
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种凭借数量或体型控制群落结构的状况
senses.example: The kelp's dominance shapes every layer of the coastal community.
senses.exampleCN: 海带的优势地位塑造了沿岸群落的每一层。
senses.why: Ecology extends the social image to a community without a ruler: dominance is measured by biomass, cover, or competitive exclusion. One species takes the high point of the canopy.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把社会意象延伸到没有统治者的群落：优势度用生物量、盖度或竞争排斥来量度。一个物种占据了冠层的高点。

senses.title: Genetic dominance: one allele masks another
senses.titleCN: 显性：一个等位基因遮盖另一个
senses.definition: the property of an allele that produces its trait even when only one copy is present
senses.definitionCN: 某一等位基因即使只有一份也能表现出其性状的性质
senses.example: The dominance of the brown-eye allele explains the family's pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 褐眼等位基因的显性解释了这一家族的遗传模式。
senses.why: Mendel's terms were borrowed from ordinary language: a dominant factor 'rules' the visible outcome, while the recessive one steps back. Dominance here is about expression, not power over other organisms.
senses.whyCN: 孟德尔的术语借自日常语言：显性因子“统治”可见结果，隐性因子则退到幕后。这里的 dominance 指表现与否，不是对别的生物的支配。

senses.title: Market dominance: one firm sets the terms
senses.titleCN: 市场主导：一家企业定下条件
senses.definition: the ability of a firm or product to set prices or standards because rivals are weak
senses.definitionCN: 由于对手弱小，某企业或产品得以定价格、定标准的能力
senses.example: Regulators examined whether the platform's dominance blocked new entrants.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构审查该平台的支配地位是否阻挡了新进入者。
senses.why: When dominance is used in competition law it becomes a threshold with legal consequences. The mountain image turns into market share plus the power to act independently of rivals.
senses.whyCN: 在竞争法中，dominance 变成一个会带来法律后果的门槛。高山意象变成市场份额，加上“可以不看对手脸色行事”的能力。

senses.title: Behavioural dominance: the top of a pecking order
senses.titleCN: 行为支配：啄序顶端的位次
senses.definition: the rank an animal holds in a group, granting priority access to food or mates
senses.definitionCN: 动物在群体中的位次，使其优先获得食物或配偶
senses.example: A single male's dominance decides who feeds first.
senses.exampleCN: 一只雄性的支配地位决定谁先进食。
senses.why: Ethology turned dominance into a measurable rank, because priority is observable even without any symbolic authority. The noun then names a position in a queue rather than a personality.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为学把 dominance 变成可测量的位次，因为“优先权”即使没有象征权威也能观察到。于是这个名词指队列中的位置，而不是性格。

senses.title: Military dominance: control of a space or region
senses.titleCN: 军事支配：对某空间或区域的控制
senses.definition: the capacity to control territory, air, or sea so that rivals cannot operate freely
senses.definitionCN: 控制陆地、空域或海域，使对手无法自由行动的能力
senses.example: Air dominance allowed the convoy to move by daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 制空权使车队得以在白天行进。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word in practical use: dominari describes a master's hold over a household, and a commander's hold over a region repeats the same relation at a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词在实际使用中最古老的一层：dominari 描述主人对家宅的掌控，而指挥官对区域的掌控只是把同一关系放大。

senses.title: Lateral dominance: the hand or side that leads
senses.titleCN: 惯用侧优势：起主导作用的手或一侧
senses.definition: the tendency of one hand, eye, or side of the body to lead in skilled movement
senses.definitionCN: 在精细动作中一只手、一只眼或身体一侧起主导作用的倾向
senses.example: Tests of manual dominance placed her firmly on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 手部优势测试把她明确归入右手型。
senses.why: The 'ruling' sense is scaled down to the body: one side takes command in writing or throwing. It shows how far the metaphor can shrink while keeping the same 'one part leads' structure.
senses.whyCN: “统治”义被缩小到身体：写字或投掷时由一侧“发号施令”。这说明该隐喻可以缩到多小，却仍保持“其中一部分领先”的结构。

intro.en: Dominance is an English noun, first recorded in the early 19th century, built from dominant plus -ance; it is not a classical Latin noun. Dominant descends from Latin dominari 'to rule', from dominus 'master'. The link between dominus and domus 'house' is generally accepted but not certain.
intro.cn: dominance 是英语自己造的名词，最早见于 19 世纪初，由 dominant 加 -ance 构成，并非古典拉丁语名词。dominant 出自拉丁语 dominari“统治”，再上为 dominus“主人”。dominus 与 domus“房屋”的联系一般被认为是成立的，但并非定论。

items.en: Dominance in digital markets becomes a standard concern in competition policy, attached to platforms rather than states.
items.cn: 数字市场中的支配地位成为竞争政策的常规议题，被安到平台而非国家身上。

items.en: Ecology, genetics and ethology each give dominance a technical definition: species cover, allele expression, group rank.
items.cn: 生态学、遗传学与动物行为学各自给 dominance 一个技术定义：物种盖度、等位基因表现、群体位次。

items.en: The English noun dominance is recorded, formed on dominant plus -ance. Before it, English used the rarer dominancy.
items.cn: 英语名词 dominance 见于记载，由 dominant 加 -ance 构成。在它之前，英语用的是更少见的 dominancy。

items.en: Latin dominari 'to rule' yields the present participle dominans, stem dominant-. Dominus 'master, lord' is generally derived from domus 'house', 'the one who owns the house'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dominari“统治”给出现在分词 dominans，词干为 dominant-。dominus“主人、家主”一般认为出自 domus“房屋”，即“拥有房屋的那个人”。

items.en: domus comes from PIE *dem- 'house, household', the same root that gives domestic, domicile and domain; dominari therefore starts from household power, not from military power.
items.cn: domus 一般认为出自原始印欧语 *dem-“房屋、家户”（重构形式），同一词根给出 domestic、domicile、domain；因此 dominari 的起点是家户之权，而非军事之权。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives and one accidental neighbour; the second compares words that share only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分真正的同族词与一个偶然撞形的词；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: the act or process of dominating. It stresses the doing, while dominance stresses the resulting position.
entries.definitionCN: 支配的行为或过程。它强调“做”，而 dominance 强调由此形成的位置。

entries.definition: a masked cloak, or a playing piece. The cloak sense comes through French from Latin dominus as a title for a priest; it never passed through the 'rule' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 化装斗篷；多米诺骨牌。斗篷义经法语来自拉丁语 dominus 作为对神职人员的称谓，从未经过“统治”这一义线。

entries.definition: an evil spirit. It comes from Greek daimon 'divine power, lesser god', and only resembles dominance in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 恶灵。它出自希腊语 daimon“神力、次要的神”，与 dominance 只是拼写相像。

entries.definition: the state of being highest in authority. It is stronger and more total than dominance, often political or military.
entries.definitionCN: 权威上的至高地位。它比 dominance 更强、更彻底，常用于政治或军事。

entries.definition: the fact of being widespread. It counts frequency, not power; dominance implies control as well as abundance.
entries.definitionCN: 普遍存在的程度。它计频率而非权力；dominance 除数量外还含控制。

entries.definition: the recognised right to command. It is legitimate power, where dominance may be mere strength.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认的指挥权。它是正当的权力，而 dominance 可能只是实力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dominance is dominant plus -ance; the suffix names a state, so it is 'the state of being dominant'.
normal.cn: dominance 是 dominant 加 -ance；后缀表示状态，所以它就是“处于支配的状态”。

normal.en: The root dominus 'master' also gives dominate, dominion, domain and predominate.
normal.cn: 词根 dominus“主人”还给出 dominate、dominion、domain、predominate。

normal.en: dominus is generally traced to domus 'house', so dominance began as household power before it became battlefield power.
normal.cn: dominus 一般认为出自 domus“房屋”，所以 dominance 先有家户之权，后有战场之权。

normal.en: Genetics borrowed the word for an allele that 'rules' what you can see; recessive alleles step back.
normal.cn: 遗传学借这个词指“统治”可见性状的等位基因；隐性等位基因则退到幕后。

normal.en: Dominance is not domination: -ance is the position, -ation is the act.
normal.cn: dominance 不等于 domination：-ance 是位置，-ation 是行为。

abstract.en: Picture one peak above a ring of hills: no hill is abolished, but every path still leads toward the shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈丘陵中耸起一座主峰：没有哪座丘陵被消灭，但每条小路都通向那片阴影。

abstract.en: The same peak appears as a ruling party, a canopy species, a visible allele, a market leader, a top ape, an air fleet, or a writing hand.
abstract.cn: 同一座主峰可以显形为执政党、冠层物种、可见等位基因、市场领先者、群体首位的猿、制空机队，或写字的那只手。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps one structure: one part leads, the rest arrange themselves around it.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保持同一结构：一个部分领先，其余围绕它排布。

examples.en: The firm's dominance in the market drew the attention of regulators.
examples.cn: 这家公司在市场上的支配地位引起了监管机构的注意。

examples.en: In this forest, one tree species has clear dominance in the canopy.
examples.cn: 在这片森林里，一个树种在冠层中具有明显的优势。

examples.en: The study tracked dominance ranks among the wolves for three winters.
examples.cn: 这项研究追踪了狼群中的支配位次长达三个冬天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多米能事」——多一米就能压住别人，站得更高 → dominance 支配地位、优势

root: 拉丁语 dominari“统治”＝dominus“主人、家主”＋动词后缀；dominus 一般认为出自 domus“房屋”（原始印欧语 *dem-“家户”）。英语 dominance＝dominant＋-ance（状态名词后缀），核心是“一个部分高过其余、发号施令”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one shape: a single peak above a field. What changes is the field — politics, a discipline, a community, a genome, a market, a group, a theatre of war, or the body itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保持同一形状：一片场域之上的一座主峰。变化的只是场域——政坛、学科、群落、基因组、市场、群体、战区，或身体本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one peak stands above the surrounding hills and every path bends toward its shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座主峰高过周围丘陵，每条小路都弯向它的阴影。

branches.en: POWER: dominus rules a household; a commander rules a region. Same relation, larger room.
branches.cn: 权力：dominus 治理家宅，指挥官治理区域。关系相同，房间更大。

branches.en: TOP POSITION: prominence in a field can exist without anyone obeying, as a peak needs no subjects.
branches.cn: 最上位：领域中的显著地位可以在无人服从时存在，正如山峰不需要臣民。

branches.en: COMMUNITY WEIGHT: in ecology the peak is measured in biomass and cover, not in commands.
branches.cn: 群落重量：在生态学中，主峰用生物量与盖度衡量，而不是用命令。

branches.en: VISIBLE TRAIT: in genetics one allele rules the phenotype while the other stays silent.
branches.cn: 可见性状：在遗传学中，一个等位基因统治表型，另一个保持沉默。

branches.en: MEASURED RANK: market share, pecking order, and the leading hand all reduce the peak to a rank or a score.
branches.cn: 可测位次：市场份额、啄序、惯用侧，都把主峰化约为一个位次或分值。

intro.en: Dominance is dominant plus -ance. The suffix -ance, from Latin -antia, names a state or quality; English coined the noun in the 19th century rather than inheriting it whole from Latin.
intro.cn: dominance 是 dominant 加 -ance。后缀 -ance 出自拉丁语 -antia，表示状态或性质；这个名词是英语在 19 世纪自造，而非整体继承自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is dominus 'master, lord', with the verb dominari 'to rule' and its participle dominant-. The same base gives dominion, domain and predominate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 dominus“主人、家主”，动词 dominari“统治”及其分词 dominant-。同一词基给出 dominion、domain、predominate。

items.meaningCN: 处于支配、优势的状态（-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: Its dominance lasted until a rival cut prices.
items.exampleCN: 它的支配地位一直持续到对手降价。

items.meaning: ruling, prevailing, or expressed over another allele
items.meaningCN: 支配的；占优势的；显性的
items.example: Blue is the dominant colour in the painting.

items.meaning: to rule, control, or tower over
items.example: The tower dominates the old harbour.

items.meaning: the act or process of dominating
items.meaningCN: 支配、控制的行为或过程（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The region suffered decades of foreign domination.
items.exampleCN: 该地区遭受了数十年的外国统治。

items.meaning: territory or authority under one ruler
items.example: The island was once a distant dominion.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛曾是遥远的领地。

items.meaning: to be the strongest or most common element
items.meaningCN: 占主导；占多数（pre- 表示“在前、高于”）
items.example: Oak predominate on the lower slopes.
items.exampleCN: 橡树在下坡地带占主导。

items.meaningCN: 占主导地位的；最显著的
items.example: Grey was the predominant tone of the room.
items.exampleCN: 灰色是这个房间的主色调。

items.meaning: bossy, controlling others by force of character
items.example: His domineering manner silenced the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 他专横的作风让会场安静下来。

items.meaning: the area a person or group controls
items.example: Tax policy lies in the domain of the finance ministry.
items.exampleCN: 税收政策属于财政部的职权范围。

items.meaning: relating to the household or to one's own country
items.meaningCN: 家庭的；国内的（与 domus“房屋”同根）
items.example: Domestic flights resumed after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨后国内航班恢复。

latinEntries.meaning: master, lord, owner of a household
to rule, to have dominion over

latinEntries.meaningCN: 统治着的；占优势的；dominant 的直接来源

definition_zh: 占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的
definition_en: having the greatest power or influence, describing a gene that shows its effect, or standing out most clearly
core_image: 长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都顺着它的方向说话
scene: 本地出租车市场里，一家公司的车标随处可见。One company has become dominant in the local taxi market.
sceneCN: 这里 dominant 是「占主导地位的」（第 1 个义项：在某个范围内拥有最大的权力或影响）；句意是有一家公司在本地出租车市场占了主导地位。

pos.zh: 占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的

senses.title: Holding the most power
senses.definition: having the greatest power, influence or share within a group, market or place
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、市场或地方拥有最大的权力、影响或份额
senses.example: Two firms dominate the market, and both are dominant in pricing.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司主导着市场，二者在定价上都占主导地位。
senses.why: Latin dominus was the master of a household, and dominans described the one who masters; dominant is the state of being that master in a group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dominus 是一家之主，dominans 描述「正在当家」的人；dominant 就是一个群体里处于这种「主人」状态。

senses.title: Expressed in genetics
senses.definition: describes a gene or trait that appears in the offspring even when only one copy is inherited
senses.definitionCN: 描述只需继承一份就能在后代身上表现出来的基因或性状
senses.example: Brown eyes are dominant over blue eyes in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个家族里，棕眼对蓝眼是显性的。
senses.why: The stronger gene behaves like the master of the household: as long as it is present, its effect is what the body shows.
senses.whyCN: 较强的基因像一家之主：只要它在场，身体表现出来的就是它的效果。

senses.title: Most noticeable
senses.definition: standing out most clearly in a view, a design or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 在景色、设计或音乐中最清晰地显露出来的
senses.example: The dominant colour of the room is a deep green.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的主色调是深绿色。
senses.why: What stands highest or appears most often catches the eye first, so it takes over the scene as a master takes over a room.
senses.whyCN: 最高的东西或出现最多的东西最先抓住目光，于是它像主人占据屋子一样占据了整个画面。

intro.en: Dominant is the present participle of Latin dominari, to rule, from dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根是 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domus meant house or household, and it also gave dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，并生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule or to have mastery over others.
items.cn: dominari 意为「统治、支配他人」。

items.en: The present participle dominans described someone or something that is ruling at that moment.
items.cn: 现在分词 dominans 描述此刻正在起支配作用的人或物。

items.en: Old French dominant carried the adjective into English usage.
items.cn: 古法语 dominant 把这个形容词带入英语用法。

items.en: English used it for political and social power before science borrowed it for genes.
items.cn: 英语先把它用于政治与社会权力，后来科学才借去指基因。

items.en: The word now also names the most visible colour, note or feature.
items.cn: 今天这个词也用来指最显眼的颜色、音符或特征。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Latin dominus root; the near-meaning group gathers words for power and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着拉丁语 dominus 词根；近义组收的是表示权力与突出地位的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to rule, control or be the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「支配、控制、占首要地位」，与 dominant 同根。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being dominant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势、支配地位」，指处于 dominant 的状态。

entries.definition: Most common or most noticeable; formed with the prefix pre-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占优势的、主要的」，由前缀 pre- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: Most important or most successful at a particular time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「领先的、最重要的」，强调位置靠前。

entries.definition: Having the power to direct or restrain others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「控制性的、起支配作用的」，强调施加约束。

entries.definition: The largest or most important of several things; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「主要的」，在若干事物中最大或最重要，语气更平实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the places dominance actually shows.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配地位真正显现的场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master of a house; dominant is the one acting as master.
normal.cn: dominus 是一家之主，dominant 就是正在当家的那一个。

normal.en: Dominari means to rule, so dominant describes whoever rules the group.
normal.cn: dominari 意为统治，dominant 描述统治这个群体的那一方。

normal.en: A dominant gene speaks loudest even when it is alone.
normal.cn: 显性基因即使只有一份，声音也最响。

normal.en: A dominant colour is the one the eye notices before all others.
normal.cn: 主色调就是眼睛先于其他颜色注意到的那个颜色。

normal.en: Pre- plus dominant gives predominant, a near twin meaning most common.
normal.cn: pre- 加 dominant 得到 predominant，意思接近「最常见、最占优势」。

abstract.en: Picture one chair at the end of a long table, slightly taller than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌尽头有一把椅子，比其余的都略高一点。

abstract.en: Picture one green wall making every other colour in the room look pale.
abstract.cn: 想象一面绿墙让屋里其他颜色都显得淡了。

abstract.en: Picture a single voice that everyone else unconsciously follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音，其他所有人都不自觉地跟着它走。

examples.en: English is the dominant language in international business.
examples.cn: 英语是国际商务中的主导语言。

examples.en: The dominant feature of the valley is a long ridge.
examples.cn: 这个山谷最突出的特征是那道长长的山脊。

examples.en: In this species, dark feathers are dominant over pale ones.
examples.cn: 在这个物种里，深色羽毛对浅色羽毛是显性的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多密难」——人一多、关系一密，就难分高下；最后站上风的那个就是 dominant。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominans，是 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主），再往前是 domus（房子、家户）。因此 dominant 本义是「像主人一样当家、压过别人」，后扩展指显性基因与最突出的特征。

sensesIntro.en: From a master of a household to a ruling firm, a loud gene and the colour that takes over a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一家之主，到主导市场的公司，再到声音最响的基因和占满屋子的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair at the head of the table that everyone turns toward.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都朝向它。

branches.en: POWER: the first sense is the social and economic mastery of a group or market.
branches.cn: 权力线：第一个义项是群体或市场中的社会与经济支配力。

branches.en: HEREDITY: the same mastery appears in a gene that overrides its partner.
branches.cn: 遗传线：同样的支配力出现在压过配对基因的显性基因上。

branches.en: ATTENTION: whatever stands out most takes over the eye's field.
branches.cn: 注意线：最突出的东西占据视野。

branches.en: Power and visibility overlap: the strongest feature is usually the one seen first.
branches.cn: 权力与可见度重叠：最强的特征通常也是最先被看见的。

branches.en: Social dominance and genetic dominance share the image of a master that cannot be ignored.
branches.cn: 社会支配与基因显性共享同一幅画面：一个无法被忽视的主人。

intro.en: Dominant is a Latin present participle in -ans, built on dominus, master of a house.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语以 -ans 结尾的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主）。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, dominus and dominari are recorded; the title dominus also survives in church language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、dominus 与 dominari 均有记录；dominus 这一称呼也保留在教会用语中。

items.example: The household is the base of the image.
items.exampleCN: 家户是这幅画面的基底。

items.example: The master sits at the head of the table.
items.exampleCN: 一家之主坐在长桌尽头。

items.example: The verb names the act of ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指统治的动作。

items.example: It became the English adjective dominant.
items.exampleCN: 它变成了英语形容词 dominant。

items.example: It forms dominant from the participle.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成 dominant 这一形容词。

items.example: The firm holds dominance in the region.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在该地区占支配地位。

items.example: One team dominated the match.
items.exampleCN: 一支队伍控制了整场比赛。

items.example: It forms predominant.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」

senses.title: To control people or places

senses.exampleCN: 几家大公司支配着航运业。
senses.why: The verb comes from dominari, to rule as a master of the house, so dominating is making others live under your direction.

senses.title: To be the main feature
senses.definition: to be the most important, noticeable or frequent part of something

senses.exampleCN: 有关风暴的消息占据了当晚新闻的主要部分。
senses.why: Whatever occupies the largest share behaves like the master of a room: it sets the tone for everything else.
senses.whyCN: 占据最大份额的东西就像屋子的主人，别的都要跟着它定调。

senses.title: To tower above a place

senses.why: A tower that fills the view from every street acts like a master overlooking a household, so the verb extends to height.
senses.whyCN: 从每条街望过去都占满视野的塔，就像俯视家户的主人，于是这个动词又扩展到高度。

intro.en: Dominate is the English verb built on Latin dominari, to rule, and on dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominate 是英语动词，建立在拉丁语 dominari（统治）与 dominus（一家之主）之上。

items.en: Domus, house or household, is the oldest word in the family.
items.cn: domus（房子、家户）是这一族里最古老的词。

items.en: Dominus named the master of the household and later any lord or owner.
items.cn: dominus 指一家之主，后来泛指主人或所有者。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule, to exercise mastery over people or things.
items.cn: dominari 意为统治，对人施加支配。

items.en: The participle dominatus described something ruled or controlled.
items.cn: 分词 dominatus 描述被统治、被控制的状态。

items.en: English formed the verb dominate from the Latin stem; exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出动词 dominate，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from people to markets, conversations and towers on a skyline.
items.cn: 词义从人扩展到市场、谈话，以及天际线上的塔。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the domin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of control and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着 domin 词干；近义组收的是表示控制与突出地位的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing whoever or whatever dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占主导地位的」，描述正在支配的那一方。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of dominating.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配、统治」，指支配的行为或状态。

entries.definition: A person or thing that dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配者」，指施行支配的人或物。

entries.definition: To direct or restrain something; it stresses management rather than superiority.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「控制、管理」，强调管理而非地位高低。

entries.definition: To prove stronger in the end, often after a struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「占上风、最终取胜」，常含经过较量之意。

entries.definition: To be more important or noticeable than something else, or to cast shade over it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使相形见绌、遮蔽」，兼有更重要与投下阴影两义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the three arenas where dominating happens.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配发生的三种场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master, so dominate is to act as that master.
normal.cn: dominus 是主人，dominate 就是扮演这个主人。

normal.cn: domination 与 dominator 直接从同一词干变来。

normal.en: Markets, talks and games can all be dominated by one side.

normal.cn: 塔高耸于天际线，是因为从每条街望过去都占满视野。

normal.en: The passive form be dominated by means the power lies with someone else.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be dominated by 表示权力在别人手里。

examples.cn: 一家连锁店主导着这座城市的咖啡市场。

examples.en: The argument dominated dinner conversation for an hour.
examples.cn: 这场争论占据晚餐谈话长达一小时。

core.cn: 核心意象：一座塔，影子伸到镇上的每一条街。

branches.cn: 人物与市场线：第一个义项是对他人的直接支配。

branches.en: THE SHARE: the second sense is dominance measured in attention or quantity.
branches.cn: 份额线：第二个义项是以注意力或数量衡量的主导。

branches.en: HEIGHT: the third sense is physical dominance over a view.
branches.cn: 高度线：第三个义项是在视野中的物理性高踞。

branches.en: Power over people and power over a conversation are two scales of the same mastery.
branches.cn: 对人的支配与对谈话的支配，是同一股当家之势的两种尺度。

branches.en: Whatever fills the view or the talk is simply the most dominant thing present.
branches.cn: 占满视野或占满谈话的东西，都只是当下最占主导的那一个。

intro.en: Donation comes from Latin donatio, a giving, built on donum, gift, and donare, to give.
intro.cn: donation 来自拉丁语 donatio（给予），其根为 donum（礼物）与 donare（给）。

items.en: The root behind donum is generally reconstructed as a word for giving; its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: donum 背后的词根一般重构为表示「给」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Donum meant a gift, something handed over without payment.
items.cn: donum 指礼物，即无偿交出的东西。

items.en: Donare meant to give, present or grant.
items.cn: donare 意为「给、赠予、授予」。

items.en: Donatio named the act of giving and also the gift itself in legal language.
items.cn: donatio 既指给予的行为，在法律用语里也指赠与之物。

items.en: Old French donation carried the word into English with its charitable tone.
items.cn: 古法语 donation 把这个词带入英语，同时带来慈善色彩。

items.en: Modern medicine added blood and organ donation to the older sense of giving money.
items.cn: 现代医学在「捐钱」这一旧义之外，又加上献血与器官捐献。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin giving root; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of contribution.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「给」的词根；近义组收的是其他形式的贡献。

senses.exampleCN: 一头驴驮着口袋走上狭窄的山道。
senses.why: The word named the familiar working animal of farms and hill paths, the one that carries what people cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指农庄与山道上最常见的工作牲口，也就是替人驮东西的那一只。

senses.title: A foolish or stubborn person
senses.definition: a foolish or stubborn person, used informally and often as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或固执的人，属非正式用法，常带侮辱意味
senses.example: Don't be a donkey and sign without reading it.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯傻看都不看就签字。
senses.why: The animal's reputation for stubbornness turned its name into a mild insult for a person who will not listen.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物以固执出名，名字便成了对不肯听话之人的轻蔑称呼。

senses.title: Dull hard work
senses.definition: used in the phrase donkey work for tiring, repetitive work that others avoid
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 donkey work，指别人不愿干的累人而重复的工作
senses.example: The interns did the donkey work of sorting old files.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生干了整理旧档案这类苦差事。
senses.why: The animal that carries loads without complaint supplies the image for work that is heavy and repetitive.
senses.whyCN: 那种默默驮重物的牲口，正好为繁重又重复的工作提供了画面。

intro.en: Donkey appeared in English in the eighteenth century and its origin is uncertain, though several explanations exist.
intro.cn: donkey 在十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定，虽有几种解释但都未定论。

items.en: The older word for the animal was ass, from Latin asinus, and it is unrelated to donkey.
items.cn: 这种动物早先叫 ass，来自拉丁语 asinus，与 donkey 没有词源关系。

items.en: Donkey is first recorded in the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: donkey 最早在十八世纪有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to dun, a dull brown colour, plus a suffix; this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与 dun（暗淡的褐色）加后缀联系起来，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: Another suggestion derives it from a proper name such as Duncan, but no explanation is proven.
items.cn: 另一种说法认为它来自 Duncan 之类的人名，但没有任何解释得到证实。

items.en: The informal sense of a foolish person and the phrase donkey work both spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「蠢人」的口语义与 donkey work 这一说法都在十九世纪流行起来。

items.en: The animal name now also supplies compounds such as donkey jacket and donkey's years.
items.cn: 这个动物名今天还提供 donkey jacket 与 donkey's years 等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on the animal name; the near-meaning group names other load-bearing beasts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是围绕这个动物名构成的复合说法；近义组收的是其他驮运牲口。

entries.definition: Tiring, repetitive work that few people want to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「苦差事」，指几乎没人愿意干的累人重复工作。

entries.definition: A short heavy work jacket, originally worn by labourers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「工装夹克」，最初是体力劳动者穿的厚短外套。

entries.definition: A very long time, used in informal British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 习语，义为「很久、多年」，属非正式英式说法。

entries.definition: The older English word for a donkey, also used for a foolish person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「驴」，也指蠢人；是这种动物的旧称。

entries.definition: The offspring of a donkey and a horse, also used for a stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骡」，也指固执的人；是驴与马的后代。

entries.definition: A small donkey, especially one used in Spanish-speaking regions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小毛驴」，多用于西班牙语地区。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the animal's real working life and the phrases English built from its name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这种动物真实的工作生活，以及英语由它名字造出的说法。

normal.en: The older word was ass, so donkey is a newer name for the same beast.
normal.cn: 旧称是 ass，donkey 只是同一头牲口后来的新名字。

normal.en: Donkey work is the heavy, repetitive part nobody wants.
normal.cn: donkey work 就是没人愿意干的繁重重复部分。

normal.en: A donkey jacket is work clothing, not something worn by an animal.
normal.cn: donkey jacket 是工装，不是驴穿的外套。

normal.en: Donkey's years means a long time, not an animal's age.
normal.cn: donkey's years 指很久，不是动物的岁数。

normal.en: Calling a person a donkey is an informal insult about stubbornness.
normal.cn: 把人叫作 donkey，是关于固执的非正式侮辱。

abstract.en: Picture long ears beside a well, refusing to take one more step.
abstract.cn: 想象井边一双长耳朵，怎么也不肯再走一步。

abstract.en: Picture two sacks of corn strapped to a small back on a steep path.
abstract.cn: 想象陡峭山道上，两袋玉米绑在一副小小的背上。

abstract.en: Picture a worker carrying the dull load while others talk.
abstract.cn: 想象别人在说话，一个工人却扛着那份枯燥的重活。

examples.en: The donkey carried water up the hill every morning.
examples.cn: 那头驴每天早上驮水上山。

examples.en: Someone has to do the donkey work before the event.
examples.cn: 活动之前总得有人干那些苦差事。

examples.en: I have not seen that shop for donkey's years.
examples.cn: 我很久没见那家店了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「当骑」——山路上驮着东西、当坐骑的那头牲口，就是 donkey。

root: donkey 于十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定；较旧的同类词是 ass（拉丁语 asinus）。常见假说把它与表示暗褐色的 dun 加后缀联系起来，也有来自人名的说法，均未获证实。驴的固执形象又派生出「蠢人」义与 donkey work 等说法。

sensesIntro.en: One animal name gives the load carrier, a stubborn person, and the heavy work nobody wants.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动物名，既给出驮物的牲口，也给出固执的人，还给出没人愿干的繁重活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small long-eared animal carrying sacks up a steep path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头长耳朵的小牲口，驮着口袋走在陡坡上。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the first sense is the working donkey on farm and hill paths.
branches.cn: 动物线：第一个义项是农庄与山道上的役用驴。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the second sense transfers the animal's stubborn image to a person.
branches.cn: 人物线：第二个义项把这种动物的固执形象移到人身上。

branches.en: THE WORK: the third sense turns patient load carrying into a phrase for dull labour.
branches.cn: 工作线：第三个义项把默默驮重变成指枯燥劳动的说法。

branches.en: The beast and the burden explain each other: the animal is named for the work it does.
branches.cn: 牲口与重活互相解释：这种动物正是因它所干的活而被使用。

branches.en: A stubborn person and an unpleasant task share the same stubborn animal image.
branches.cn: 固执的人与难缠的活共享同一幅固执动物的画面。

intro.en: Donkey has no Latin root; English builds its phrases and compounds from the animal name itself.
intro.cn: donkey 没有拉丁词根，英语直接用这个动物名搭出短语与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for a donkey was asinus, but it is not a cognate, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里驴叫 asinus，但它并非同源词，所以这里不列拉丁词族。

Dun is one suggested source of the name.
items.exampleCN: dun 是这个名字的一种假想来源。

items.example: The ending has no agreed meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾没有公认含义。

items.example: Two donkeys grazed on the slope.
The donkey work took all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这些苦差事干了一下午。

items.example: He wore a dark donkey jacket.

items.example: It has been donkey's years since we met.
The older word was ass.

definition_zh: n. 捐赠者；捐款人；供血者；器官捐献者；施主（半导体）
definition_en: a person or organisation that gives money, blood, organs or aid, or an impurity that supplies electrons
core_image: 一张姓名栏空着的支票；冷柜里一排贴着标签的血袋；一张签过名的卡片放在钱包里驾照旁边；一只印着援助机构标记的板条箱；一张晶格图上多余电子被标为自由

sceneCN: 这里 donor 是「捐款人」（第 1 个义项：向某事业捐钱的人或机构）；句意：医院感谢了那位匿名捐款人。图中可辨识物件：支票、空白的姓名栏、医院柜台、祝福字条。

pos.zh: 捐赠者；捐款人；供血者；器官捐献者；施主（半导体）

senses.title: A money giver
senses.definition: a person or body that gives money to a cause
senses.definitionCN: （名词）向某事业捐钱的人或机构
senses.example: The hospital thanked its anonymous donor.
senses.exampleCN: 医院感谢了那位匿名捐款人。
senses.why: A cheque with the name line left blank.
senses.whyCN: 一张姓名栏空着的支票。

senses.title: A blood giver
senses.definition: a person who gives blood for medical use
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为医疗用途献血的人
senses.example: The clinic needs donors of the rarest type.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所需要最稀有血型的供血者。
senses.why: A row of labelled bags in a cold cabinet.
senses.whyCN: 冷柜里一排贴着标签的血袋。

senses.title: An organ giver
senses.definition: a person whose organs are used for transplant
senses.definitionCN: （名词）器官被用于移植的人
senses.example: The transplant waited for a matching donor.
senses.exampleCN: 移植手术在等待配型相合的捐献者。
senses.why: A signed card carried in a wallet beside a licence.
senses.whyCN: 一张签过名的卡片放在钱包里、驾照旁边。

senses.title: An aid body
senses.definition: an organisation that supplies goods or aid
senses.definitionCN: （名词）提供物资或援助的机构
senses.example: Several donors funded the new library wing.
senses.exampleCN: 几家捐赠机构资助了图书馆新翼。
senses.why: A crate stamped with the mark of a foreign aid body.
senses.whyCN: 一只印着外国援助机构标记的板条箱。

senses.title: A semiconductor impurity
senses.definition: an impurity that supplies free electrons in a semiconductor
senses.definitionCN: （名词）半导体中提供自由电子的杂质
senses.example: Phosphorus acts as a donor in silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 磷在硅中起施主作用。
senses.why: A lattice diagram with one extra electron marked loose.
senses.whyCN: 一张晶格图，其中一个多余电子被标为自由。

intro.en: Donor is don- plus -or, the one who does; it goes back through Old French doneur to Latin donator, a giver, from donare, to give as a gift.
intro.cn: donor 由 don- 加 -or「做…的人」构成；它经古法语 doneur 追溯到拉丁语 donator「给予者」，源自 donare「作为礼物给予」。

items.en: Latin donum means a gift.
items.cn: 拉丁语 donum 意为礼物。

items.en: Donare means to give as a gift.
items.cn: donare 意为作为礼物给予。

items.en: Donator means a giver.
items.cn: donator 意为给予者。

items.en: Old French doneur names the one who gives.
items.cn: 古法语 doneur 指给予的人。

items.en: The word comes to name blood and organ givers.
items.cn: 这个词转而指血液与器官的给予者。

items.en: Donor also names an impurity supplying electrons.
items.cn: donor 也指提供电子的杂质。

note.en: Donor is the one who gives; its look-alikes share the gift root, and its neighbours name other givers and the opposite receiver.
note.cn: donor 是给予的那一方；形近词共用「礼物」词根，近义词则是别的给予者，以及相反的接受方。

dict_mnemonic.text: donor ＝ don（礼物，拉丁语 donum）＋ -or（名词后缀，表示「做…的人」）＝「送礼的人」。与之相对，-ee 表示「受…的人」，所以受赠人是 donee；捐出的东西或行为是 donation，动作本身是 donate。

definition_zh: n. 厄运；劫数；毁灭；末日审判；（古）判决 v. 注定（失败或死亡）；判定
definition_en: death or a terrible fate that cannot be avoided, or to make such a fate certain
core_image: 灰天空下一道干涸的河床与一排空屋；一道细缝在混凝土墙上越裂越宽；一本日历上剩下的每个日期都被划掉；一杆画出来的天平在深坑上方称量灵魂
scene: 坝上那道细缝越裂越宽，山谷里的人开始搬东西。The crack in the dam spelled doom for the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 doom 是「毁灭」（第 2 个义项：死亡、毁灭或希望的终结）；句意：坝上的裂缝意味着山谷的毁灭。图中可辨识物件：混凝土坝、越裂越宽的缝、搬东西的人、山谷房屋。

pos.zh: 厄运；劫数；毁灭；末日审判
注定（失败或死亡）；判定

senses.title: An unavoidable fate
senses.definition: a terrible fate that cannot be escaped
senses.definitionCN: （名词）无法逃脱的可怕命运
senses.example: The village accepted its doom without a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 村子一声不响地接受了它的厄运。
senses.why: A dry riverbed and a line of empty houses under a grey sky.
senses.whyCN: 灰天空下一道干涸的河床与一排空屋。

senses.title: Death or ruin
senses.definition: death, destruction or the end of hope
senses.definitionCN: （名词）死亡、毁灭或希望的终结
senses.example: The crack in the dam spelled doom for the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 坝上的裂缝意味着山谷的毁灭。
senses.why: A thin crack widening across a concrete wall.
senses.whyCN: 一道细缝在混凝土墙上越裂越宽。

senses.title: Make a fate certain
senses.definition: to make a bad outcome certain for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某人或某物的坏结果成为定局
senses.example: The injury doomed the season for the team.
senses.exampleCN: 那次伤病注定了球队的赛季。
senses.why: A calendar with every remaining date crossed out.
senses.whyCN: 一本日历，剩下的每个日期都被划掉。

senses.title: The last judgement
senses.definition: the final judgement of souls in religious belief
senses.definitionCN: （名词）宗教信仰中对灵魂的最终审判
senses.example: The fresco shows the doom of the wicked.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅湿壁画描绘了恶人的末日审判。
senses.why: A painted scale weighing souls above a dark pit.
senses.whyCN: 一杆画出来的天平在深坑上方称量灵魂。

senses.title: An old legal sentence
senses.definition: a judicial sentence or decree, in older use
senses.definitionCN: （名词）旧用法中的司法判决或法令
senses.example: The chronicle records the doom pronounced by the king.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记载了国王宣布的判决。
senses.why: A sealed scroll read aloud from a stone step.
senses.whyCN: 一卷封了印的文书在石阶上被宣读。

intro.en: Doom began as Old English dom, a judgement or decree, from the verb deman, to judge, which survives today as deem; once a sentence is read out the fate is fixed, so the word slid from judgement to ruin.
intro.cn: doom 起初是古英语 dom「判决、法令」，源自动词 deman「判定」，这个动词今天以 deem 的形式留存；判决一经宣读命运就定了，于是词义从「判决」滑向「毁灭」。

items.en: Old English dom means judgement or decree.
items.cn: 古英语 dom 意为判决、法令。

items.en: The related verb deman means to judge.
items.cn: 相关动词 deman 意为判定。

items.en: Middle English doom keeps the sense of a sentence passed.
items.cn: 中古英语 doom 保留「宣判」的意思。

items.en: The word shifts from the sentence to the fate it fixes.
items.cn: 词义从「判决」转向判决所定的命运。

items.en: The verb means to condemn to a fate.
items.cn: 动词意为判定某人落入某种命运。

items.en: Doom now names ruin, and doomsday the end of the world.
items.cn: doom 现在指毁灭，doomsday 指世界末日。

note.en: Doom is a fate fixed by a sentence; its look-alikes share the old judge stem, and its neighbours name other kinds of destined end.
note.cn: doom 是被判决定下的命运；形近词共用古老的「判定」词干，近义词则是别的注定的结局。

examples.en: The crack in the dam spelled doom for the valley.

examples.cn: 那幅湿壁画描绘了恶人的末日审判。

dict_mnemonic.text: doom 在古英语里本是「判决」（dom），动词 deman 是「判定」，今天英语的 deem 还留着这个意思。判决一旦宣读，命运就定了，于是 doom 从「判决」变成「厄运、毁灭」；动词则是「注定要失败」。doomsday 就是「审判日」。

root: 古英语 dom（判决）→ deman（判定）→ 中古英语 doom（判决；命运）→ 现代 doom（厄运；注定）

definition_zh: 宿舍；宿舍楼；宿舍房间；宿舍的
definition_en: a student residence hall, a room inside it, or a word used before another noun for student housing
core_image: 熄灯后的走廊，一串钥匙轻轻碰在一起
scene: 熄灯后的走廊只剩脚步声，钥匙在锁孔里转了半圈。She tiptoed back to the dorm after the library closed.
sceneCN: 这里 dorm 是「学生宿舍」（第 1 个义项：学生住的宿舍楼，dormitory 的口语简称）；句意是图书馆关门后她踮着脚回到了宿舍。

pos.zh: 宿舍；宿舍楼；宿舍房间
