senses.title: A student residence hall
senses.definition: a building where students live during term time, the informal short form of dormitory
senses.definitionCN: 学期内学生居住的楼房，是 dormitory 的口语简称
senses.example: The dorm stands next to the sports field.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍楼紧挨着运动场。
senses.why: Students cut the long Latin-derived dormitory down to four letters, but kept the building and its communal life in the short form.
senses.whyCN: 学生把源自拉丁语的长词 dormitory 缩成四个字母，但这一简称仍然保留了那栋楼和集体生活。

senses.title: A room in a hall
senses.definition: a single room used by a student inside a residence hall
senses.definitionCN: 宿舍楼里供一名学生使用的单个房间
senses.example: His dorm is small but has a desk by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他的宿舍不大，但窗边有一张书桌。
senses.why: The building name slides down to the room, since students speak of the place they actually sleep in.
senses.whyCN: 楼房的名称滑落到房间上，因为学生说的是自己真正睡觉的那个地方。

senses.title: Of student housing
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe things connected with student housing
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一个名词前，描述与学生住宿有关的事物
senses.example: Dorm food is cheap but rarely exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍饭菜便宜，但很少让人惊喜。
senses.why: A place name easily becomes a label, so dorm attaches to food, life and mates as if it were an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地名很容易变成标签，于是 dorm 像形容词一样贴到 food、life 与 mate 前面。

intro.en: Dorm is a clipped form of dormitory, from Latin dormitorium, a sleeping place.
intro.cn: dorm 是 dormitory 的缩略形式，后者来自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方）。

items.en: Dormire meant to sleep, and it sits at the base of the whole family.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡觉」，是整个词族的基底。

items.en: Dormitorium named a sleeping room, especially one shared by several people.
items.cn: dormitorium 指睡觉的房间，尤指多人共用的房间。

items.en: English dormitory first named a shared sleeping room in a monastery or school.
items.cn: 英语 dormitory 最初指修道院或学校里共用的睡房。

items.en: Universities expanded dormitories into large residence buildings for students.
items.cn: 大学把 dormitory 扩展成大型学生宿舍楼。

items.en: The clipped form dorm spread in student speech and in campus notices.
items.cn: 缩略形式 dorm 在学生口语与校园告示中流行起来。

items.en: Dorm now appears in compounds such as dorm room and dorm life.
items.cn: 今天 dorm 出现在 dorm room、dorm life 这类复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin sleep root; the near-meaning group names other shared housing.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「睡」的词根；近义组收的是其他集体住处。

entries.definition: A large building or room; at universities it can mean a residence.

normal.en: Dormire is to sleep; dormitorium is the place for it.

examples.en: The dorm is quiet during the exam week.

examples.en: She keeps a small plant on her dorm windowsill.

examples.en: Dorm life taught him to share a kitchen.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逗梦」——宿舍是学生一起做梦、互相逗趣的地方，dorm 就是宿舍。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the third sense uses the place name before other nouns.

branches.en: Building and room share the name because students move between the two every day.
branches.cn: 整栋楼与单个房间共用一个名字，因为学生每天都在两者之间来回。

branches.en: The room becomes a label: dorm food is food experienced in that room.

definition_zh: 休眠；休眠状态；（行业等的）停滞期
definition_en: a temporary state in which growth, development or activity almost stops and resumes when conditions improve
core_image: 一只上了锁的抽屉里放着一粒种子和一只芽，抽屉外的季节轮转，抽屉里一切暂停
scene: 干土里，一粒种子把外壳收紧，内部的代谢慢到几乎测不出，等到雨水渗下来才重新吸水。Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
sceneCN: 这里 dormancy 指「生长与代谢近乎停止、条件改善后可恢复的状态」（第 1 个义项：生物休眠状态）；句意为深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。图中可辨识物件：土粒、种皮、滴落的水、细小的胚根。

pos.zh: 休眠；休眠状态；休眠期

derivatives.zh: 安息；被称为安眠的死亡

senses.title: Suspended growth or activity
senses.titleCN: 生长与活动近乎停止的状态
senses.definition: a temporary condition in which an organism's growth or metabolism slows almost to a stop and later resumes
senses.definitionCN: 生物的生长或代谢几乎停止、之后又能恢复的暂时状态
senses.example: Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
senses.exampleCN: 深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。
senses.why: Latin dormire meant 'to sleep', so dormancy is the noun of a sleeping body, applied to seeds and spores that show no movement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dormire 意为「睡」，因此 dormancy 是「睡着的身体」的名词，用于看不出动静的种子与孢子。

senses.title: The period of suspended life
senses.definition: the interval between entering dormancy and the trigger that ends it
senses.definitionCN: 从进入休眠到触发其结束之间的间隔
senses.example: The dormancy of these acorns lasts until the first wet autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这些橡子的休眠持续到第一个多雨的秋天。
senses.why: The noun can measure time as well as name a state, because dormancy is defined by its duration.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能量时间也能命名状态，因为休眠正是由持续时长来界定的。

senses.title: Seed dormancy
senses.definition: the condition in which a ripe seed will not germinate even with water and warmth until cold, light or time breaks the block
senses.definitionCN: 成熟的种子即使有水有温度也不萌发，须经低温、光照或时间才解除阻断的状态
senses.example: Seed dormancy spreads germination across several seasons instead of one week.
senses.exampleCN: 种子休眠把萌发分散到几个季节，而不是挤在一周内。
senses.why: A seed that waited for the right season would die in a false spring, so the block is a safety device.
senses.whyCN: 若种子在假春天萌发就会死去，因此这道阻断是一重保险。

senses.title: Bud and tuber dormancy
senses.definition: the winter or storage rest in which buds, tubers and bulbs will not sprout until chilling or warmth releases them
senses.definitionCN: 芽、块茎与球茎在冬季或储藏期不发芽，直到低温或回暖解除的状态
senses.example: Potato dormancy is broken by storing the tubers in cool, bright conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 把块茎放在凉爽明亮的环境中即可打破马铃薯的休眠。
senses.why: Here the sleeper is a bud rather than a whole plant, but the same rule holds: no growth until the signal arrives.
senses.whyCN: 这里睡着的是芽而非整株植物，但规则相同：信号不到就不生长。

senses.title: Bacterial and spore dormancy
senses.definition: the extremely low-activity state of spores and dormant bacteria, which can revive after long storage
senses.definitionCN: 孢子与休眠细菌活动极低、经长期存放仍可复苏的状态
senses.example: Spore dormancy can outlast the laboratory that first described it.
senses.exampleCN: 孢子的休眠可以比最初描述它的实验室活得更久。
senses.why: At this scale dormancy means a toughened coat and a nearly stopped metabolism, not sleep in any animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 在这个尺度上，休眠意味着坚硬的外壳与几乎停摆的代谢，而不是动物意义上的睡眠。

senses.title: Latency of a virus
senses.definition: the quiet phase in which a virus stays inside a cell without producing new particles or symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 病毒留在细胞内、不产生新颗粒也不引起症状的安静阶段
senses.example: Viral dormancy keeps the infection hidden for years.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒的潜伏让感染隐藏多年。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the seed image: the agent is present but not growing, and can wake when conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了种子的意象：病原在场却不生长，条件一变就可能醒来。

senses.title: A quiet stretch in a market or field
senses.definition: a figurative period in which an industry, market or project shows almost no activity but is not finished
senses.definitionCN: 行业、市场或项目几乎无活动、却并未终结的比喻性时期
senses.example: The dormancy of the housing market ended with a single cut in interest rates.
senses.exampleCN: 房地产市场的一段沉寂，因一次降息而结束。
senses.why: The metaphor drops the biology and keeps the shape: low activity, preserved capacity, later revival.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻舍弃生物学内容，只保留外形：低活动、保有能力、日后复苏。

senses.title: The depth of the resting state
senses.definition: the degree to which a resting organism resists waking, measured by how hard the block is to break
senses.definitionCN: 休眠中的生物抗拒苏醒的程度，以阻断有多难打破来衡量
senses.example: Biologists rate dormancy by the chilling hours needed to release it.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家按解除休眠所需的低温小时数来划分休眠深度。
senses.why: Once dormancy can be measured, it acquires a scale, and the noun comes to name a point on that scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦休眠可以被测量，它就有了刻度，这个名词也就用来指刻度上的某一点。

intro.en: Dormancy is an eighteenth-century English noun from dormant, which descends through French from Latin dormire 'to sleep'. The Latin verb is the source of a whole family of sleeping words.
intro.cn: dormancy 是十八世纪英语名词，来自 dormant，后者经法语源自拉丁 dormire「睡」。这个拉丁动词是一整族「睡眠」词的源头。

items.en: Dormire meant 'to sleep'. Its deeper origin is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for sleep, marked with an asterisk because it is rebuilt rather than recorded.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡」。其更早来源一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示睡眠的重构词根；因是重建而非有记录，故带星号。

items.en: A dormitorium was a sleeping room. English dormitory descends from it, which is why the word for a hall of beds and the word for a sleeping seed look related.
items.cn: dormitorium 是「寝室」。英语 dormitory 由此而来，所以「宿舍」与「休眠的种子」看起来沾亲。

items.en: Old French used dormant, the present participle of dormir, for 'sleeping'. English borrowed the adjective in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 dormir 的现在分词 dormant 表示「睡着的」。英语在十三世纪借入这个形容词。

items.en: The abstract noun dormancy is recorded in the eighteenth century, formed with -cy on the model of other state nouns. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词 dormancy 见于十八世纪，依照其他状态名词的模式加 -cy 构成。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Botany gave the word its modern precision by distinguishing true dormancy, which is internally controlled, from quiescence, which is forced by conditions.
items.cn: 植物学赋予这个词现代意义上的精确性：真正的休眠由内部控制，而静止状态由外部条件迫使。

items.en: Twentieth-century writing extended dormancy to viruses, markets and institutions, always keeping the promise of a later waking.
items.cn: 二十世纪的写作把 dormancy 扩展到病毒、市场与机构，始终保留「日后会醒来」的许诺。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin sleeping root that are easily confused; group two holds rival terms for a life on hold.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「睡」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示生命暂停的竞争性术语。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the state; dormancy is the noun, so one says seeds are dormant but seeds show dormancy.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该状态的形容词；dormancy 是名词，因此说种子处于休眠，而不说种子表现出休眠。

entries.definition: From Latin dormitorium 'sleeping room'; it names a place for sleeping, not a biological pause.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dormitorium「寝室」，指睡觉的场所，不是生物性暂停。

entries.definition: From Old French dormeor 'sleeping room', applied to the roof window that lights such a room.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 dormeor「寝室」，用来指给该房间采光的屋顶窗。

entries.definition: From Latin dormitio 'a sleeping', used in theology for a death described as falling asleep.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dormitio「入睡」，神学中用来指被称为「睡着」的死亡。

entries.definition: A slowdown caused directly by external conditions, with no internal clock; the organism resumes the moment conditions improve.
entries.definitionCN: 由外部条件直接造成的放慢，没有内部时钟；条件一好就立刻恢复。

entries.definition: A deep seasonal dormancy of winter; dormancy is the wider category that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季的深度季节性休眠；dormancy 是包含它的更大类别。

entries.definition: The state of being present but not expressed, common for viruses and diseases; it stresses concealment rather than slowed growth.
entries.definitionCN: 存在却不表现的状态，常用于病毒与疾病；强调隐藏而非生长减慢。

entries.definition: A general halt in change or flow, from Greek stasis 'standing'; it need not imply a living thing that can wake.
entries.definitionCN: 变化或流动的总体停止，来自希腊 stasis「站立」；不必然暗示能醒来的活物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dormire is 'to sleep', so dormancy is the noun of sleep: a sleeping that a seed or spore can perform.
normal.cn: dormire 是「睡」，所以 dormancy 是「睡」的名词：种子或孢子也能进行的一种睡。

normal.en: The family runs dormant, dormancy, dormitory, dormer, dormition, dormitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dormant、dormancy、dormitory、dormer、dormition、dormitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the biology: seed dormancy, break dormancy, deep dormancy, bud dormancy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生物学用法：种子休眠、打破休眠、深度休眠、芽休眠。

normal.en: Dormancy is internally controlled; quiescence is forced from outside, a distinction worth memorising as a pair.
normal.cn: 休眠由内部调控，静止由外部迫使；这对区别值得成对记住。

normal.en: The same root shows up in dormitory: a room for sleep, a seed for sleeping.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 dormitory：一间用来睡的房间，一粒用来睡的种子。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with its pendulum lifted and held, not removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的摆锤被抬起按住，而不是被拆掉。

abstract.en: Picture a letter sealed and put away, still readable when opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被密封收起，打开时仍可读。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with the lights off but the stock still on the shelves.
abstract.cn: 想象一家关了灯的店，货架上的存货仍在。

examples.en: Deep dormancy keeps the seeds viable for years in dry soil.
examples.cn: 深度休眠使这些种子在干燥土壤中多年仍有活力。

examples.en: Seed dormancy spreads germination across several seasons instead of one week.
examples.cn: 种子休眠把萌发分散到几个季节，而不是挤在一周内。

examples.en: Viral dormancy keeps the infection hidden for years.
examples.cn: 病毒的潜伏让感染隐藏多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多梦」——睡得多、梦得多，生长也停了 → 休眠

root: 拉丁 dormire「睡」+ 名词后缀 -ncy（经由 dormant 构成抽象状态名词）；dormire 更早一般追溯到原始印欧语表示睡眠的重构词根（星号形式为重构），确切音形存疑。英语 dormancy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: life is put on hold without being ended. The gesture begins with seeds and buds, widens to spores and viruses, then to markets, and finally becomes a measurable depth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把生命挂起，却不终结它。这个动作从种子与芽开始，扩到孢子与病毒，再到市场，最后成为一种可测量的深度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked drawer holding a seed and a bud while the seasons turn outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只上锁的抽屉里放着种子与芽，抽屉外季节轮转。

branches.en: THE GENERAL PAUSE: life continues without growth, and the noun also measures how long the pause lasts.
branches.cn: 总体暂停：生命继续却不生长，名词还计量暂停持续多久。

branches.en: SEEDS AND BUDS: the coat or the chilling requirement decides when growth may restart.
branches.cn: 种子与芽：种皮或需冷量决定生长何时可以重启。

branches.en: SMALL AND HIDDEN: spores toughen and viruses go quiet, both present but not multiplying.
branches.cn: 微小而隐蔽：孢子变硬、病毒转静，都在场却不增殖。

branches.en: MARKET QUIET: an industry borrows the pause and waits for demand to return.
branches.cn: 市场沉寂：行业借用这个暂停，等待需求回来。

branches.en: MEASURED DEPTH: once the block can be timed, dormancy becomes a quantity.
branches.cn: 可测的深度：一旦阻断可以被计时，休眠就成为一个量。

intro.en: Dormancy is built on a Latin verb of sleeping; the same root reappears in rooms and windows, which makes the family unusually easy to read.
intro.cn: dormancy 建立在一个表示「睡」的拉丁动词上；同一词根还出现在房间与窗户里，使这个词族格外容易读。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire 'to sleep' gives dormitorium 'sleeping room', dormitio 'a sleeping' and the adjective dormitivus; the English abstract noun adds -cy to dormant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dormire「睡」生出 dormitorium「寝室」、dormitio「入睡」与形容词 dormitivus；英语抽象名词则在 dormant 后加 -cy。

definition_zh: 休眠的；蛰伏的；潜伏的；闲置的
definition_en: in a state in which growth or activity is temporarily stopped while life or capacity remains
core_image: 一截埋在土里的枝条看上去像枯木，刮开表皮，里面仍是青色
scene: 天冷以后，院子角落的球茎一直不出芽，直到春天温度回升。The bulbs stay dormant in the cold frame until spring warmth returns.
sceneCN: 这里 dormant 指「生长暂停、但仍存活并可恢复的」（第 1 个义项：植物休眠的）；句意为球茎在冷床里保持休眠，直到春天回暖。图中可辨识物件：冷床玻璃、覆土的球茎、枯叶、温度计。

pos.zh: 休眠的；蛰伏的；潜伏的；闲置的（作定语或表语）

derivatives.zh: 安息；被称为安眠的死亡

senses.title: Resting but alive in a plant
senses.definition: describing a seed, bulb or bud that shows no growth yet remains alive until conditions change
senses.definitionCN: 形容种子、球茎或芽暂不生长，却仍然存活，直到条件改变
senses.example: The bulbs stay dormant in the cold frame until spring warmth returns.
senses.exampleCN: 球茎在冷床里保持休眠，直到春天回暖。
senses.why: Latin dormire 'to sleep' gives the adjective its picture: alive, unmoving, and able to wake.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dormire「睡」给这个形容词一幅图：活着、不动、能醒。

senses.title: In winter torpor, of an animal
senses.definition: describing an animal whose body temperature and activity have dropped for the cold season
senses.definitionCN: 形容动物在寒冷季节体温与活动都已下降
senses.example: The frogs lie dormant under the frozen mud for months.
senses.exampleCN: 这些蛙在冻泥下休眠数月。
senses.why: The adjective does not name the season itself, so it can describe any animal rest, not only winter sleep.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不命名季节本身，因此可描述任何动物休息，不限于冬眠。

senses.title: Hidden and not multiplying, of a virus
senses.definition: describing a virus or infection that is present in the body without producing symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 形容病毒或感染存在于体内却不产生症状
senses.example: The virus can remain dormant in nerve cells for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒能在神经细胞中潜伏数十年。
senses.why: Latency is the medical version of the same image: something is there, quiet, and possibly able to wake.
senses.whyCN: 潜伏是同一意象的医学版本：某物在场、安静，且可能醒来。

senses.title: A volcano that is quiet but not extinct
senses.titleCN: 休眠火山（安静但未熄灭）
senses.definition: describing a volcano that has not erupted for a long time but still has a magma supply
senses.definitionCN: 形容长期未喷发、却仍有岩浆供给的火山
senses.example: The dormant volcano supports farms on its fertile lower slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 这座休眠火山肥沃的低坡上种着庄稼。
senses.why: Geology borrows the biological word because the mountain is not dead, only asleep between eruptions.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用这个生物词，因为山并未死，只是在两次喷发之间睡着。

senses.title: An account or device left unused
senses.definition: describing an account, service or machine that is still valid but has been unused for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 形容账户、服务或机器仍然有效，却长期无人使用
senses.example: The bank closed the dormant account after five years without a transaction.
senses.exampleCN: 五年没有交易后，银行关闭了这个休眠账户。
senses.why: Nothing has died: the account still exists, it simply has no activity, exactly like a sleeping body.
senses.whyCN: 并没有东西死去：账户仍然存在，只是没有活动，正像睡着的身体。

senses.title: An economy or market that is not moving
senses.definition: describing trade, hiring or construction that has slowed almost to a stop but has not collapsed
senses.definitionCN: 形容贸易、招聘或建设几乎停住却并未崩盘
senses.example: Construction stayed dormant until the new loan scheme began.
senses.exampleCN: 在新贷款方案启动前，建筑业一直停滞。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the contrast between alive and active: the sector is alive, but not moving.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「活着」与「活动」的对照：行业活着，却不动。

senses.title: Present but not yet expressed
senses.definition: describing a capacity, feeling or talent that exists but has not yet shown itself
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种能力、情感或才华存在却尚未显露
senses.example: A dormant talent for languages woke when she moved abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她移居国外后，潜伏的语言才能被唤醒。
senses.why: The abstract use treats an ability as a seed: it is fully there, waiting for the right condition.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把能力当作种子：它完整地在，只等合适的条件。

senses.title: A right or clause not currently enforced
senses.definition: describing a legal right or provision that exists but is not being applied at present
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项法律权利或条款存在，但目前未被施行
senses.example: The lease keeps a dormant clause that can be revived by written notice.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约保留一条休眠条款，可经书面通知恢复效力。
senses.why: Law needs a word for a right that sleeps without dying, and the biological adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个词来形容「睡着却没死」的权利，这个生物形容词正好合用。

intro.en: Dormant comes through Old French dormant, the present participle of dormir, from Latin dormire 'to sleep'. English borrowed it in the thirteenth century, first for sleeping people and later for sleeping nature.
intro.cn: dormant 经古法语 dormant（dormir 的现在分词）来自拉丁 dormire「睡」。英语在十三世纪借入，先形容睡着的人，后形容沉睡的自然界。

items.en: Dormire meant 'to sleep'. Its deeper origin is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for sleep, a form marked with an asterisk because it is rebuilt rather than attested.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡」。其更早来源一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示睡眠的重构词根；因是重建而非有文献佐证，故带星号。

items.en: The frequentative dormitare 'to be sleepy, to drowse' also existed; it lies behind words such as dormitive rather than behind dormant itself.
items.cn: 拉丁还有反复动词 dormitare「困倦、打瞌睡」，它是 dormitive 一类词的来源，而非 dormant 的直接来源。

items.en: Old French formed the present participle dormant from dormir. English took the whole adjective rather than building it anew.
items.cn: 古法语由 dormir 构成现在分词 dormant。英语整体借入这个形容词，而不是重新构造。

items.en: The first English uses describe sleeping persons or animals; the transferred sense for inactive things appears later.
items.cn: 英语最早用例描述睡着的人或动物；转指不活动之物的用法出现得更晚。

items.en: Botany and geology extended the word to seeds, buds and volcanoes, where 'asleep' means alive or still capable of acting.
items.cn: 植物学与地质学把这个词扩展到种子、芽与火山；在这些领域，「睡着」意味着仍活着或仍能发作。

items.en: Banking and commerce added dormant accounts and dormant companies in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, keeping the same promise of possible revival.
items.cn: 银行与商业在十九至二十世纪补充了休眠账户、休眠公司等说法，保留同样的「可能复苏」许诺。

note.en: Group one holds members of the Latin sleeping family that differ by suffix; group two holds adjectives for something present but not active.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「睡」词族、仅后缀不同的成员；第二组是表示「存在但不活动」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun of the same state; one says a seed is dormant, or that a seed is in dormancy.
entries.definitionCN: 同一状态的名词；可说种子处于休眠，或说种子处于休眠状态。

entries.definition: From Latin dormitorium 'sleeping room'; it is a place, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dormitorium「寝室」，是地点而非状态。

entries.definition: The roof window that lights a sleeping room, from Old French dormeor.
entries.definitionCN: 给寝室采光的屋顶窗，来自古法语 dormeor。

entries.definition: A theological term for a death described as sleep; the root is the same but the reference is final.
entries.definitionCN: 神学中把死亡说成入睡的术语；词根相同，但所指是终结性的。

entries.definition: Present but not yet visible or active, as in latent heat or a latent infection; it has no seasonal rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 存在却尚未显现或活动，如潜热或潜伏感染；没有季节节律。

entries.definition: Simply not active, with no promise that life or function is preserved; dormant always implies a surviving core.
entries.definitionCN: 只是不活动，不保证生命或功能仍被保存；dormant 总暗示核心仍存活。

entries.definition: Resting because conditions forbid activity, ready to resume at once; dormant often implies an internal brake.
entries.definitionCN: 因条件不允许而休息，条件一好立刻恢复；dormant 常暗示内部制动。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for nightly rest; for volcanoes or accounts it is a looser metaphor than dormant.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指夜间休息的词；用于火山或账户时，比喻不如 dormant 严谨。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dormant is the sleeping adjective: a sleeping seed, a sleeping volcano, a sleeping account.
normal.cn: dormant 就是「睡着的」形容词：睡着的种子、睡着的火山、睡着的账户。

normal.en: The family runs dormant, dormancy, dormitory, dormer, dormition, dormitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dormant、dormancy、dormitory、dormer、dormition、dormitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: lie dormant, dormant volcano, dormant account, dormant seed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：处于休眠、休眠火山、休眠账户、休眠种子。

normal.en: A dormant thing is not dead: that single contrast separates it from extinct or ruined.
normal.cn: dormant 之物并未死：正是这一点把它与「灭绝」「毁坏」区分开。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: DOR-mant, like DOR-mant volcano.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：DOR-mant，如休眠火山。

abstract.en: Picture a switch in the off position with the power still connected.
abstract.cn: 想象一个处于关闭位置的开关，电源却仍接者。

abstract.en: Picture a bear's slow breath measured against a snowdrift.
abstract.cn: 想象熊的缓慢呼吸与雪堆相对照。

abstract.en: Picture a violin kept in its case, tuned and ready.
abstract.cn: 想象一把收在琴盒里的提琴，调好了音，随时可拉。

examples.en: The bulbs stay dormant in the cold frame until spring warmth returns.
examples.cn: 球茎在冷床里保持休眠，直到春天回暖。

examples.en: The virus can remain dormant in nerve cells for decades.
examples.cn: 这种病毒能在神经细胞中潜伏数十年。

examples.en: The bank closed the dormant account after five years without a transaction.
examples.cn: 五年没有交易后，银行关闭了这个休眠账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多梦的」——多梦的人睡得很沉，叫也叫不醒 → 休眠的、蛰伏的

root: 古法语 dormant（dormir 的现在分词）→ 拉丁 dormire「睡」；更早一般追溯到原始印欧语表示睡眠的重构词根（星号形式为重构），确切音形存疑。英语 dormant。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one contrast: alive but not moving. The adjective starts with plants and animals, moves to viruses and volcanoes, then to accounts, markets, talents and legal clauses.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个对照展开：活着却不动。这个形容词从植物与动物开始，转到病毒与火山，再转到账户、市场、才能与法律条款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut stem that looks dead outside but is green under the bark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一截外表像枯木、刮开树皮却仍是青色的枝条。

branches.en: LIVING REST: plants and animals keep their core while growth and movement stop.
branches.cn: 活着的休息：植物与动物在生长与活动停止时保住核心。

branches.en: HIDDEN FORCE: a virus waits inside a cell and a volcano waits under a mountain.
branches.cn: 隐藏的力量：病毒在细胞内等待，火山在山体下等待。

branches.en: UNUSED CAPACITY: an account or a market keeps its structure but shows no motion.
branches.cn: 未用的能力：账户或市场保住结构，却不显示运动。

branches.en: UNEXPRESSED ABILITY: a talent is fully present before it is ever seen.
branches.cn: 未显露的才能：才华在被看见之前已完整存在。

branches.en: SLEEPING RIGHT: a clause stays valid while enforcement waits.
branches.cn: 睡着的权利：条款保持有效，执法暂时等待。

intro.en: Dormant is a Latin present participle carried into English through French, so its suffix marks an ongoing state rather than an action.
intro.cn: dormant 是经法语进入英语的拉丁现在分词，因此它的后缀标记的是持续状态，而非动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire 'to sleep' builds dormitare 'to drowse', dormitorium 'sleeping room' and dormitio 'a sleeping'; English adds -cy, -y and -ion to make the modern family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dormire「睡」构成 dormitare「打瞌睡」、dormitorium「寝室」与 dormitio「入睡」；英语再加 -cy、-y、-ion 形成现代词族。

senses.title: A student residence
senses.definition: a building where students sleep and live during term time
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学期内睡觉与生活的楼房
senses.example: The oldest dormitory on campus has been rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 校园里最老的宿舍楼已经重建。
senses.why: Latin dormitorium was a sleeping place, and universities turned it into a building that belongs to student life.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dormitorium 本是睡觉的地方，大学把它变成属于学生生活的整栋建筑。

senses.title: Shared housing for workers
senses.definition: a large shared bedroom or building for workers, nurses or other groups
senses.definitionCN: 供工人、护士或其他群体居住的大型共用寝室或楼房
senses.example: The nurses share a dormitory near the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们合住医院附近的一栋集体宿舍。
senses.why: The sleeping-place word serves any group that lives together for work, not only students.
senses.whyCN: 这个「睡觉之处」的词不只服务学生，也服务任何因工作而住在一起的人群。

senses.title: A dormitory town
senses.definition: a residential area where people live but travel elsewhere for work, used in British English
senses.definitionCN: 人们居住但去别处上班的住宅区，属英式英语用法
senses.example: The village became a dormitory suburb of the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子变成了首都的睡城郊区。
senses.why: A place where people mainly sleep and then leave each morning is like a whole town turned into a dormitory.
senses.whyCN: 人们主要在此睡觉、每天早晨又离开的地方，就像整座城镇变成了一间宿舍。

intro.en: Dormitory comes from Latin dormitorium, a sleeping place, built on dormire, to sleep.
intro.cn: dormitory 来自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方），其根为 dormire（睡）。

items.en: Dormire meant to sleep and supplied the verb root for the whole family.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡觉」，为整族词提供动词词根。

items.en: Dormitorium named a sleeping room, especially a shared one in a monastery.
items.cn: dormitorium 指睡房，尤指修道院里共用的寝室。

items.en: The word entered English for a shared sleeping room in religious houses.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，先指宗教团体里共用的寝室。

items.en: Schools and universities used it for large buildings that housed many students.
items.cn: 学校与大学用它指容纳许多学生的大型楼房。

items.en: British planners applied it to dormitory towns and suburbs where people only sleep.
items.cn: 英国规划者把它用到人们只在此睡觉的睡城与郊区。

items.en: The clipped form dorm now competes with the full word in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语里，缩略形式 dorm 已与全称并用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin sleep root; the near-meaning group names other group housing.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「睡」的词根；近义组收的是其他集体住处。

entries.definition: The short everyday form of dormitory.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宿舍」，是 dormitory 的日常缩略形式。

entries.definition: A window built into a sloping roof.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「屋顶窗」，与 dormitory 同出拉丁语 dormire。

entries.definition: A rare term meaning sleep-inducing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「催眠的；安眠药」，较少使用。

entries.definition: The formal American name for a student dormitory.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「学生宿舍楼」，是美式正式说法。

entries.definition: Cheap shared lodging for travellers, students or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅舍、青年宿舍」，供旅行者、学生或工人廉价合住。

entries.definition: A private house that provides rooms and meals for paying residents.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「寄宿公寓」，指提供房间与伙食收费的私人住宅。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dormire family and the three places it came to describe.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dormire 词族，以及它后来描述的三类地方。

normal.en: Dormire is to sleep, so a dormitory is a place built around sleep.
normal.cn: dormire 是睡觉，dormitory 就是以睡觉为中心的地方。

normal.en: The suffix -ory marks a place, as in dormitory.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ory 标记地点，dormitory 正是这样。

normal.en: Dormitory first meant a shared room in a religious house.
normal.cn: dormitory 最初指宗教团体里共用的寝室。

normal.en: The nurses' dormitory shows the word does not belong only to students.
normal.cn: 护士的集体宿舍说明这个词不只属于学生。

normal.en: A dormitory town is a whole place used mainly for sleeping.
normal.cn: 睡城就是整片地方主要只用来睡觉。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with a row of wash bags moving toward one sink.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，一排洗漱袋朝同一个水池移动。

abstract.en: Picture four hundred windows going dark at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象四百扇窗在同一时间暗下去。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet suburb where every car leaves at seven and returns at six.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静的郊区，七点车都走了，六点又都回来了。

examples.en: They met on the first day in the dormitory.
examples.cn: 他们在宿舍里第一天就认识了。

examples.en: The hospital provides a dormitory for night staff.
examples.cn: 医院给夜班员工提供集体宿舍。

examples.en: He grew up in a dormitory town outside the city.
examples.cn: 他在城外的睡城长大。

dict_mnemonic.text: dorm 是「睡」，-ory 表示地点：专门用来睡的地方，就是宿舍。

root: 源自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方），由 dormire（睡）加地点后缀 -torium 构成。英语十五世纪先指修道院或学校的共用寝室，十九世纪扩展为大型学生宿舍楼，二十世纪又被英国规划者用来指人们只在夜里睡觉的睡城。

sensesIntro.en: From a shared sleeping room, to a student building, a workers' lodging, and finally a whole commuter town.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共用的睡房，到学生宿舍楼、工人集体宿舍，最后到整片通勤者居住的睡城。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long corridor where people carry wash bags before dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明前的长走廊，人们提着洗漱袋走动。

branches.en: STUDENTS: the first sense is the campus building for students.
branches.cn: 学生线：第一个义项是校园里供学生居住的楼。

branches.en: WORKERS: the second sense is shared housing for nurses and other staff.
branches.cn: 工薪线：第二个义项是护士与其他员工的集体宿舍。

branches.en: THE TOWN: the third sense stretches the sleeping place to a whole suburb.
branches.cn: 城镇线：第三个义项把这个睡觉之处拉伸到整片郊区。

branches.en: Students and workers share the same building type because both need cheap group lodging.
branches.cn: 学生与工人共用同一种建筑，因为两者都需要便宜的集体住宿。

branches.en: A workers' lodging and a commuter town both exist mainly for sleep.
branches.cn: 工人宿舍与睡城的存在，主要都是为了睡觉。

intro.en: Dormitory is dormire plus the Latin place suffix -torium, shortened into English -ory.
intro.cn: dormitory 是 dormire 加拉丁语地点后缀 -torium，进入英语后收为 -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire and dormitorium are recorded; dormitorius also appears as an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dormire 与 dormitorium 均有记录，dormitorius 也以形容词形式出现。

items.example: The verb is the base of the name.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一名称的基础。

items.example: The noun described a shared room.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指共用的房间。

items.example: It turns the root into dormitory.
The dormitory was full in September.
He moved into a dorm last week.
A dormer lets light into the attic.
The term is now rare and formal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词现在罕见而正式。

items.example: Three dormitories line the path.

definition_zh: 剂量；一剂；一次（不愉快的经历）；给药
definition_en: a measured amount of medicine taken at one time, an amount of something experienced, or to give medicine to someone
core_image: 一只量杯对着标签上的刻度，护士仔细核对
scene: 药瓶上贴着模糊的标签，护士拿量杯仔细对了一遍刻度。The label warns patients not to exceed the daily dose.
sceneCN: 这里 dose 是「剂量」（第 1 个义项：一次服用的、经过计量的药量）；句意是标签警告病人不要超过每日剂量。

pos.zh: 剂量；一剂；一次（不愉快的经历）
给……服药；给……加（某物）

senses.title: A measured amount of medicine
senses.definition: a measured amount of a medicine or drug taken at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次服用的、经过计量的药量
senses.example: The doctor reduced the dose after the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 第一周之后医生减少了剂量。
senses.why: Greek dosis meant a giving, and medicine turned that giving into an exact quantity measured out for one occasion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 dosis 意为「给予」，医学把这次给予变成一次称量好的精确数量。

senses.title: An unpleasant experience
senses.definition: an amount of something unpleasant that a person has to experience, such as an illness or a shock
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不得不承受的某种不快之物的分量，如疾病或惊吓
senses.example: He got a dose of flu during the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途中他得了一次流感。
senses.why: If medicine comes in doses, then anything that hits the body or the feelings can also arrive in one measured portion.
senses.whyCN: 既然药可以按剂来算，那么任何冲击身体或情绪的东西也能以一份计量好的分量到来。

senses.title: To give medicine to
senses.definition: to give a person or animal a measured amount of medicine or another substance
senses.definitionCN: 给一个人或动物服用一定量的药或其他物质
senses.example: The farmer dosed the sick calf with a bitter liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫给病牛犊喂了一种苦味的药水。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to dose is to hand over exactly the measured giving the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：dose 就是把名词所指的那份计量好的给予交出去。

intro.en: Dose comes through French from Late Latin dosis, which borrowed Greek dosis, a giving.
intro.cn: dose 经法语来自晚期拉丁语 dosis，后者借自希腊语 dosis（给予）。

items.en: Didonai meant to give, and it supplied the root for dosis.
items.cn: didonai 意为「给」，为 dosis 提供词根。

items.en: Dosis meant the act of giving or a portion given, and doctors used it for a measured portion of medicine.
items.cn: dosis 指给予的行为或给出的份额，医生用它指称量好的一份药。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed dosis directly from Greek medical writing.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语从希腊医学文献直接借入 dosis。

items.en: French dose carried the medical sense into everyday use.
items.cn: 法语 dose 把医学义带入日常使用。

items.en: English dose is recorded from the seventeenth century for a quantity of medicine.
items.cn: 英语 dose 自十七世纪有记录，指一定量的药。

items.en: The word widened to doses of flu, doses of reality and the verb to dose.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到「一次流感」「一次现实教训」，并产生动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the giving and measuring root; the near-meaning group names related medical quantities.
note.cn: 形近组共享「给予、计量」的词根；近义组收的是相关医学用量词。

entries.definition: The amount and schedule of medicine prescribed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「用量、剂量方案」，指处方规定的量与次数。

entries.definition: An instrument that measures radiation dose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剂量计」，用来测量辐射剂量的仪器。

entries.definition: An amount of medicine that is too large and dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「用药过量」，指过大而有危险的药量。

entries.definition: A general word for how much of something there is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数量」，泛指某物有多少，范围最广。

entries.definition: A part or share of something larger, often for one person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一份、份额」，指较大物中的一部分，常供一人使用。

entries.definition: A doctor's written order for medicine, including its dose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「处方」，医生开药的书面指示，其中包含剂量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Greek giving root and the measured situations where dose appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的希腊语「给」词根，以及 dose 出现的计量场景。

normal.en: Dosis means a giving, and a dose is a giving measured out.
normal.cn: dosis 意为给予，dose 就是称量好的一次给予。

normal.en: Greek didonai, to give, is the older verb behind dosis.
normal.cn: 希腊语 didonai（给）是 dosis 背后更早的动词。

normal.en: Daily dose is the amount allowed in one day.
normal.cn: daily dose 就是一天允许的量。

normal.en: A dose of flu borrows the medicine measure for an illness.
normal.cn: a dose of flu 借用药的计量来说一次流感。

normal.en: The verb dose means to hand over that measured amount.
normal.cn: 动词 dose 就是把那份计量好的量交给对方。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse lining a small cup up against a printed scale.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把一只小量杯对准印好的刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of bitter liquid held steady beside a sick animal.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺苦药稳稳地举在病畜旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a single spoonful becoming the exact limit for one day.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺药成为一天不可超过的界限。

examples.en: Take the dose with food to avoid stomach pain.
examples.cn: 随餐服用这一剂，以免胃痛。

examples.en: The nurse dosed the child every six hours.
examples.cn: 护士每六小时给孩子服一次药。

examples.en: The trip gave him a dose of cold wind and hard truth.
examples.cn: 这趟旅程给了他一阵冷风和一次现实的教训。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抖死」——剂量过大真会让人抖得厉害；所以 dose 要按刻度来。

root: 源自希腊语 dosis（给予），由 didonai（给）派生，经晚期拉丁语 dosis 与法语 dose 进入英语。本义是「给出的一份」，医学上固定为一次计量好的药量，后又引申指一次不愉快的经历，并产生动词「给药」义。

sensesIntro.en: One giving word measures medicine, measures bad experiences, and finally names the act of giving medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「给」的词，既计量药，也计量糟糕的经历，最后还指给药这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small measuring cup aligned with the marks on a bottle label.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小量杯对准药瓶标签上的刻度。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the first sense is the exact amount of a drug taken at one time.
branches.cn: 药物线：第一个义项是一次服用的精确药量。

branches.en: EXPERIENCE: the second sense measures illness or shock instead of medicine.
branches.cn: 经历线：第二个义项计量的不是药，而是疾病或冲击。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the third sense is the handing over of that measured amount.
branches.cn: 动作线：第三个义项是把那份计量好的量交出去。

branches.en: The noun and verb face each other: the dose is what the act of dosing delivers.
branches.cn: 名词与动词相对：dose 就是给药动作所交付的东西。

branches.en: Medicine and misfortune both arrive in portions one has to take.
branches.cn: 药与不幸都以人必须承受的一份份分量到来。

intro.en: Dose is a Greek-derived stem; English adds -age, -meter and over- to build its family.
intro.cn: dose 是源自希腊语的词干，英语靠 -age、-meter 与 over- 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed dosis from Greek, so the Latin entry is itself a loan word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dosis 借自希腊语，因此这条拉丁条目本身也是借词。

items.example: The Greek verb is the giving root.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊动词是「给」的词根。

items.example: Greek doctors used it for medicine.
The dose is printed on the box.
The dosage depends on body weight.
It forms dosage.
Workers wear a dosimeter.
An overdose can be fatal.
It forms dosimeter.

latinEntries.meaning: a giving, a portion of medicine
